declarations.name: spi_accepted
declarations.informal: The signals of player i on which the static-threshold searcher with threshold T stops: those with posterior mean at least T.
declarations.statement:
open Finset in
noncomputable def spi_accepted {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) : Finset (Fin S)
declarations.source:
open Finset in
/-- The signals of player `i` on which the static-threshold searcher with threshold `T` stops: those whose posterior mean reward is at least `T` (written `T * mass ≤ value`, so null signals are harmless). -/
noncomputable def spi_accepted {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) : Finset (Fin S) :=
  univ.filter fun s => T * spi_signal_mass w φ i s ≤ spi_signal_value x w φ i s
declarations.citation: Intrinsic Robustness of Prophet Inequality to Strategic Reward Signaling, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2409.18269), Sec. 2-3 (model, Definition 2.4, Proposition 3.1), Remark 4.1 and Sec. 6; formalized by the operator (Claude), 2026-10-04, for finite reward supports and finite signal sets

declarations.name: spi_accept_prob
declarations.informal: Probability that the searcher accepts player i when she reaches it.
declarations.statement:
open Finset in
noncomputable def spi_accept_prob {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) : ℝ
declarations.source:
open Finset in
/-- Probability that the searcher accepts player `i` when she reaches it. -/
noncomputable def spi_accept_prob {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) : ℝ :=
  ∑ s ∈ spi_accepted x w φ T i, spi_signal_mass w φ i s
declarations.citation: Intrinsic Robustness of Prophet Inequality to Strategic Reward Signaling, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2409.18269), Sec. 2-3 (model, Definition 2.4, Proposition 3.1), Remark 4.1 and Sec. 6; formalized by the operator (Claude), 2026-10-04, for finite reward supports and finite signal sets

declarations.name: spi_accept_value
declarations.informal: Expected reward collected from player i on the event that it is reached and accepted.
declarations.statement:
open Finset in
noncomputable def spi_accept_value {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) : ℝ
declarations.source:
open Finset in
/-- Expected reward collected from player `i` on the event that the searcher reaches and accepts it (the sum of probability times posterior mean over accepted signals). -/
noncomputable def spi_accept_value {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) : ℝ :=
  ∑ s ∈ spi_accepted x w φ T i, spi_signal_value x w φ i s
declarations.citation: Intrinsic Robustness of Prophet Inequality to Strategic Reward Signaling, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2409.18269), Sec. 2-3 (model, Definition 2.4, Proposition 3.1), Remark 4.1 and Sec. 6; formalized by the operator (Claude), 2026-10-04, for finite reward supports and finite signal sets

declarations.name: spi_reach_prob
declarations.informal: Probability that the search reaches player i: all earlier players are rejected (independence across players).
declarations.statement:
open Finset in
noncomputable def spi_reach_prob {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) : ℝ
declarations.source:
open Finset in
/-- Probability that the search reaches player `i`, i.e. every earlier player is rejected (rewards and signals are independent across players). -/
noncomputable def spi_reach_prob {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) : ℝ :=
  ∏ j ∈ univ.filter (fun j => j < i), (1 - spi_accept_prob x w φ T j)
declarations.citation: Intrinsic Robustness of Prophet Inequality to Strategic Reward Signaling, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2409.18269), Sec. 2-3 (model, Definition 2.4, Proposition 3.1), Remark 4.1 and Sec. 6; formalized by the operator (Claude), 2026-10-04, for finite reward supports and finite signal sets

declarations.name: spi_searcher_payoff
declarations.informal: The searcher's expected payoff u_s(T) under static threshold T and the players' signaling schemes.
declarations.statement:
open Finset in
noncomputable def spi_searcher_payoff {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) : ℝ
declarations.source:
open Finset in
/-- The searcher's expected payoff `u_s(T)` under the static threshold `T` and the players' signaling schemes `φ`. -/
noncomputable def spi_searcher_payoff {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, spi_reach_prob x w φ T i * spi_accept_value x w φ T i
declarations.citation: Intrinsic Robustness of Prophet Inequality to Strategic Reward Signaling, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2409.18269), Sec. 2-3 (model, Definition 2.4, Proposition 3.1), Remark 4.1 and Sec. 6; formalized by the operator (Claude), 2026-10-04, for finite reward supports and finite signal sets

declarations.name: spi_player_payoff
declarations.informal: Player i's payoff: the probability that the searcher selects it.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spi_player_payoff {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) : ℝ
declarations.source:
/-- Player `i`'s payoff: the probability that the searcher selects it. -/
noncomputable def spi_player_payoff {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) : ℝ :=
  spi_reach_prob x w φ T i * spi_accept_prob x w φ T i
declarations.citation: Intrinsic Robustness of Prophet Inequality to Strategic Reward Signaling, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2409.18269), Sec. 2-3 (model, Definition 2.4, Proposition 3.1), Remark 4.1 and Sec. 6; formalized by the operator (Claude), 2026-10-04, for finite reward supports and finite signal sets

declarations.name: spi_is_scheme
declarations.informal: A signaling scheme of one player: for every support point a probability distribution over the S signals.
declarations.statement:
open Finset in
def spi_is_scheme {K S : ℕ} (ψ : Fin K → Fin S → ℝ) : Prop
declarations.source:
open Finset in
/-- A signaling scheme of one player: for every support point, a probability distribution over the `S` signals. -/
def spi_is_scheme {K S : ℕ} (ψ : Fin K → Fin S → ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ k s, 0 ≤ ψ k s) ∧ ∀ k, ∑ s, ψ k s = 1
declarations.citation: Intrinsic Robustness of Prophet Inequality to Strategic Reward Signaling, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2409.18269), Sec. 2-3 (model, Definition 2.4, Proposition 3.1), Remark 4.1 and Sec. 6; formalized by the operator (Claude), 2026-10-04, for finite reward supports and finite signal sets

declarations.name: spi_is_equilibrium
declarations.informal: Nash equilibrium of the players' signaling game induced by a static threshold T: no player can raise its selection probability by unilaterally switching schemes.
declarations.statement: def spi_is_equilibrium {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (T : ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Nash equilibrium of the players' signaling game induced by the static threshold `T`: no player can raise its selection probability by switching to another scheme. -/
def spi_is_equilibrium {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (T : ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, spi_is_scheme (φ i)) ∧
    ∀ i (ψ : Fin K → Fin S → ℝ), spi_is_scheme ψ →
      spi_player_payoff x w (Function.update φ i ψ) T i ≤ spi_player_payoff x w φ T i
declarations.citation: Intrinsic Robustness of Prophet Inequality to Strategic Reward Signaling, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2409.18269), Sec. 2-3 (model, Definition 2.4, Proposition 3.1), Remark 4.1 and Sec. 6; formalized by the operator (Claude), 2026-10-04, for finite reward supports and finite signal sets

declarations.name: spi_prophet_value
declarations.informal: The prophet benchmark OPT = E[max_i X_i] for independent finite-support rewards.
declarations.statement:
open Finset in
noncomputable def spi_prophet_value {N K : ℕ} (x w : Fin (N + 1) → Fin K → ℝ) : ℝ
declarations.source:
open Finset in
/-- The prophet benchmark `OPT = E[max_i X_i]` for independent finite-support rewards. -/
noncomputable def spi_prophet_value {N K : ℕ} (x w : Fin (N + 1) → Fin K → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ k : Fin (N + 1) → Fin K, (∏ i, w i (k i)) * univ.sup' univ_nonempty (fun i => x i (k i))
declarations.citation: Intrinsic Robustness of Prophet Inequality to Strategic Reward Signaling, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2409.18269), Sec. 2-3 (model, Definition 2.4, Proposition 3.1), Remark 4.1 and Sec. 6; formalized by the operator (Claude), 2026-10-04, for finite reward supports and finite signal sets

declarations.name: spi_two_point_max_prob
declarations.informal: Proposition 3.1 for a two-point reward (h with probability q, else l): the largest acceptance probability achievable under threshold T (1 if T <= E[X], q(h-l)/(T-l) if E[X] < T <= h, 0 if T > h).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def spi_two_point_max_prob (h l q T : ℝ) : ℝ
declarations.source:
/-- Prop. 3.1 of arXiv:2409.18269 for a two-point reward (`h` with probability `q`, else `l`): the largest probability with which the player can get accepted under threshold `T`. -/
noncomputable def spi_two_point_max_prob (h l q T : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  if T ≤ q * h + (1 - q) * l then 1 else if T ≤ h then q * (h - l) / (T - l) else 0
declarations.citation: Intrinsic Robustness of Prophet Inequality to Strategic Reward Signaling, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2409.18269), Sec. 2-3 (model, Definition 2.4, Proposition 3.1), Remark 4.1 and Sec. 6; formalized by the operator (Claude), 2026-10-04, for finite reward supports and finite signal sets

declarations.name: spi_two_point_max_value
declarations.informal: The searcher's expected reward from a two-point player using an optimal scheme (E[X] if T <= E[X], T times the pooling probability if E[X] < T <= h, 0 above h).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def spi_two_point_max_value (h l q T : ℝ) : ℝ
declarations.source:
/-- The searcher's expected reward from a two-point player using an optimal scheme (no information if `T ≤ E[X]`, pooling the top mass to posterior mean exactly `T` otherwise). -/
noncomputable def spi_two_point_max_value (h l q T : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  if T ≤ q * h + (1 - q) * l then q * h + (1 - q) * l else if T ≤ h then T * (q * (h - l) / (T - l)) else 0
declarations.citation: Intrinsic Robustness of Prophet Inequality to Strategic Reward Signaling, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2409.18269), Sec. 2-3 (model, Definition 2.4, Proposition 3.1), Remark 4.1 and Sec. 6; formalized by the operator (Claude), 2026-10-04, for finite reward supports and finite signal sets

declarations.name: spi_accept_reduction
declarations.informal: The acceptance probability, accepted value and posterior-mean constraint of any scheme depend only on accepted masses A_k in [0, w_ik] satisfying T sum A_k <= sum A_k x_ik.
declarations.statement:
open Finset in
lemma spi_accept_reduction {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) (hw : ∀ k, 0 ≤ w i k) (hφ : spi_is_scheme (φ i)) :
    ∃ A : Fin K → ℝ, (∀ k, 0 ≤ A k ∧ A k ≤ w i k) ∧ spi_accept_prob x w φ T i = ∑ k, A k ∧
      spi_accept_value x w φ T i = ∑ k, A k * x i k ∧ T * ∑ k, A k ≤ ∑ k, A k * x i k
declarations.source:
open Finset in
/-- The accepted probability, accepted value and the posterior-mean constraint of any scheme only depend on the accepted mass `A k ∈ [0, w i k]` of every support point. -/
lemma spi_accept_reduction {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) (hw : ∀ k, 0 ≤ w i k) (hφ : spi_is_scheme (φ i)) :
    ∃ A : Fin K → ℝ, (∀ k, 0 ≤ A k ∧ A k ≤ w i k) ∧ spi_accept_prob x w φ T i = ∑ k, A k ∧
      spi_accept_value x w φ T i = ∑ k, A k * x i k ∧ T * ∑ k, A k ≤ ∑ k, A k * x i k := by
  refine ⟨fun k => ∑ s ∈ spi_accepted x w φ T i, w i k * φ i k s, fun k => ⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun s _ => mul_nonneg (hw k) (hφ.1 k s)
  · show (∑ s ∈ spi_accepted x w φ T i, w i k * φ i k s) ≤ w i k
    rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
    calc w i k * ∑ s ∈ spi_accepted x w φ T i, φ i k s ≤ w i k * ∑ s, φ i k s := by
          apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left _ (hw k)
          exact Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (Finset.subset_univ _) fun s _ _ => hφ.1 k s
      _ = w i k := by rw [hφ.2 k, mul_one]
  · simp only [spi_accept_prob, spi_signal_mass]
    exact Finset.sum_comm
  · simp only [spi_accept_value, spi_signal_value, Finset.sum_mul]
    exact Finset.sum_comm
  · have h1 : T * ∑ k, ∑ s ∈ spi_accepted x w φ T i, w i k * φ i k s =
        ∑ s ∈ spi_accepted x w φ T i, T * spi_signal_mass w φ i s := by
      rw [Finset.sum_comm, Finset.mul_sum]; rfl
    have h2 : ∑ k, (∑ s ∈ spi_accepted x w φ T i, w i k * φ i k s) * x i k =
        ∑ s ∈ spi_accepted x w φ T i, spi_signal_value x w φ i s := by
      simp only [spi_signal_value, Finset.sum_mul]; exact Finset.sum_comm
    rw [h1, h2]
    exact Finset.sum_le_sum fun s hs => (Finset.mem_filter.mp hs).2
declarations.citation: step towards strategic_prophet_no_half_robust_static_threshold (no static threshold is 1/2-robust, open in Intrinsic Robustness of Prophet Inequality to Strategic Reward Signaling, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2409.18269), Remark 4.1 and Sec. 6)

declarations.name: spi_two_point_core
declarations.informal: Real-arithmetic core of Proposition 3.1 for two-point rewards: accepted masses with posterior mean at least T have total at most spi_two_point_max_prob, and attaining it pins the accepted value to spi_two_point_max_value.
declarations.statement:
lemma spi_two_point_core (h l q T a b : ℝ) (hlh : l ≤ h) (hq0 : 0 ≤ q) (hq1 : q ≤ 1)
    (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (ha1 : a ≤ q) (hb0 : 0 ≤ b) (hb1 : b ≤ 1 - q) (hc : T * (a + b) ≤ a * h + b * l) :
    a + b ≤ spi_two_point_max_prob h l q T ∧
      (spi_two_point_max_prob h l q T ≤ a + b → a * h + b * l = spi_two_point_max_value h l q T)
declarations.source:
/-- Real-arithmetic core of Prop. 3.1 for a two-point reward: accepted masses `a ≤ q` (on `h`) and `b ≤ 1 - q` (on `l`) with posterior mean at least `T` have total at most `spi_two_point_max_prob`, and attaining it pins the accepted value to `spi_two_point_max_value`. -/
lemma spi_two_point_core (h l q T a b : ℝ) (hlh : l ≤ h) (hq0 : 0 ≤ q) (hq1 : q ≤ 1)
    (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (ha1 : a ≤ q) (hb0 : 0 ≤ b) (hb1 : b ≤ 1 - q) (hc : T * (a + b) ≤ a * h + b * l) :
    a + b ≤ spi_two_point_max_prob h l q T ∧
      (spi_two_point_max_prob h l q T ≤ a + b → a * h + b * l = spi_two_point_max_value h l q T) := by
  unfold spi_two_point_max_prob spi_two_point_max_value
  split_ifs with h1 h2
  · refine ⟨by linarith, fun hP => ?_⟩
    have : a = q := by linarith
    have : b = 1 - q := by linarith
    subst_vars; ring
  · have hTl : l < T := by nlinarith
    have hTl' : 0 < T - l := by linarith
    have key : b * (T - l) ≤ a * (h - T) := by nlinarith
    refine ⟨?_, fun hP => ?_⟩
    · rw [le_div_iff₀ hTl']; nlinarith
    · rw [div_le_iff₀ hTl'] at hP
      have : a * (h - T) ≤ b * (T - l) := by nlinarith
      have hab : a + b = q * (h - l) / (T - l) := by
        rw [eq_div_iff hTl'.ne']; nlinarith
      rw [← hab]; nlinarith
  · have hab : (a + b) * (T - h) ≤ 0 := by nlinarith
    have : a + b ≤ 0 := by
      by_contra hneg; push Not at hneg
      have := mul_pos hneg (show 0 < T - h by linarith); linarith
    refine ⟨this, fun _ => ?_⟩
    have : a = 0 := by linarith
    have : b = 0 := by linarith
    subst_vars; ring
declarations.citation: step towards strategic_prophet_no_half_robust_static_threshold (no static threshold is 1/2-robust, open in Intrinsic Robustness of Prophet Inequality to Strategic Reward Signaling, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2409.18269), Remark 4.1 and Sec. 6)

declarations.name: spi_accept_prob_mem_Icc
declarations.informal: Acceptance probabilities of valid schemes on two-point rewards lie in [0, 1].
declarations.statement:
open Finset in
lemma spi_accept_prob_mem_Icc {N S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin 2 → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) (hw : ∀ k, 0 ≤ w i k) (hsum : w i 0 + w i 1 = 1) (hφ : spi_is_scheme (φ i)) :
    0 ≤ spi_accept_prob x w φ T i ∧ spi_accept_prob x w φ T i ≤ 1
declarations.source:
open Finset in
/-- Acceptance probabilities are probabilities: for a scheme and probability weights, `0 ≤ P_i ≤ 1` (stated for two-point rewards). -/
lemma spi_accept_prob_mem_Icc {N S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin 2 → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) (hw : ∀ k, 0 ≤ w i k) (hsum : w i 0 + w i 1 = 1) (hφ : spi_is_scheme (φ i)) :
    0 ≤ spi_accept_prob x w φ T i ∧ spi_accept_prob x w φ T i ≤ 1 := by
  obtain ⟨A, hA, hP, -, -⟩ := spi_accept_reduction x w φ T i hw hφ
  rw [hP, Fin.sum_univ_two]
  constructor <;> linarith [hA 0, hA 1]
declarations.citation: step towards strategic_prophet_no_half_robust_static_threshold (no static threshold is 1/2-robust, open in Intrinsic Robustness of Prophet Inequality to Strategic Reward Signaling, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2409.18269), Remark 4.1 and Sec. 6)

declarations.name: spi_two_point_bound
declarations.informal: For a two-point reward, every scheme's acceptance probability is at most spi_two_point_max_prob, and if it attains it the accepted value equals spi_two_point_max_value.
declarations.statement:
open Finset in
lemma spi_two_point_bound {N S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin 2 → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) (hlh : x i 1 ≤ x i 0) (hq0 : 0 ≤ w i 0) (hq1 : w i 0 ≤ 1)
    (hw1 : w i 1 = 1 - w i 0) (hφ : spi_is_scheme (φ i)) :
    spi_accept_prob x w φ T i ≤ spi_two_point_max_prob (x i 0) (x i 1) (w i 0) T ∧
      (spi_two_point_max_prob (x i 0) (x i 1) (w i 0) T ≤ spi_accept_prob x w φ T i →
        spi_accept_value x w φ T i = spi_two_point_max_value (x i 0) (x i 1) (w i 0) T)
declarations.source:
open Finset in
/-- For a two-point reward (`x i 0 = h ≥ x i 1 = l`, `w i 0 = q`, `w i 1 = 1 - q`), every scheme's acceptance probability is at most `spi_two_point_max_prob`, and if it attains it the accepted value equals `spi_two_point_max_value`. -/
lemma spi_two_point_bound {N S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin 2 → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) (hlh : x i 1 ≤ x i 0) (hq0 : 0 ≤ w i 0) (hq1 : w i 0 ≤ 1)
    (hw1 : w i 1 = 1 - w i 0) (hφ : spi_is_scheme (φ i)) :
    spi_accept_prob x w φ T i ≤ spi_two_point_max_prob (x i 0) (x i 1) (w i 0) T ∧
      (spi_two_point_max_prob (x i 0) (x i 1) (w i 0) T ≤ spi_accept_prob x w φ T i →
        spi_accept_value x w φ T i = spi_two_point_max_value (x i 0) (x i 1) (w i 0) T) := by
  have hw : ∀ k, 0 ≤ w i k := by
    intro k; fin_cases k
    · exact hq0
    · simp only [Fin.mk_one, hw1]; linarith
  obtain ⟨A, hA, hP, hV, hc⟩ := spi_accept_reduction x w φ T i hw hφ
  simp only [Fin.sum_univ_two] at hP hV hc
  have hA1 := hA 1
  rw [hw1] at hA1
  have core := spi_two_point_core (x i 0) (x i 1) (w i 0) T (A 0) (A 1) hlh hq0 hq1 (hA 0).1 (hA 0).2
    hA1.1 hA1.2 hc
  rw [hP, hV]
  exact core
declarations.citation: Intrinsic Robustness of Prophet Inequality to Strategic Reward Signaling, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2409.18269), Proposition 3.1 (optimal information revealing strategy under threshold T); special case of two-point rewards, finite signal sets

declarations.name: spi_two_point_pool_prob
declarations.informal: The probability with which the low value joins the accepted signal in the optimal scheme: 1 if T <= E[X], q(h-T)/((1-q)(T-l)) if E[X] < T <= h, 0 if T > h.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def spi_two_point_pool_prob (h l q T : ℝ) : ℝ
declarations.source:
/-- The probability with which the low value of a two-point reward joins the pooled (accepted) signal in the optimal scheme of Prop. 3.1: `1` if `T ≤ E[X]`, `q (h - T) / ((1 - q) (T - l))` if `E[X] < T ≤ h`, and `0` if `T > h`. -/
noncomputable def spi_two_point_pool_prob (h l q T : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  if T ≤ q * h + (1 - q) * l then 1 else if T ≤ h then q * (h - T) / ((1 - q) * (T - l)) else 0
declarations.citation: Intrinsic Robustness of Prophet Inequality to Strategic Reward Signaling, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2409.18269), Proposition 3.1 (threshold signaling: pooling probability with T = E[X | accepted]); two-point case

declarations.name: spi_two_point_scheme
declarations.informal: The optimal scheme of Proposition 3.1 for a two-point reward embedded in S signals: high value sends signal 0, low value sends signal 0 with the pooling probability and signal 1 otherwise.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def spi_two_point_scheme (S : ℕ) (h l q T : ℝ) : Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ
declarations.source:
/-- The optimal scheme of Prop. 3.1 for a two-point reward, embedded in `S` signals: the high value (index 0) always sends signal 0; the low value (index 1) sends signal 0 with probability `spi_two_point_pool_prob` and signal 1 otherwise. -/
noncomputable def spi_two_point_scheme (S : ℕ) (h l q T : ℝ) : Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ := fun k s =>
  if k = 0 then (if s.val = 0 then 1 else 0)
  else if s.val = 0 then spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T
  else if s.val = 1 then 1 - spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T else 0
declarations.citation: Intrinsic Robustness of Prophet Inequality to Strategic Reward Signaling, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2409.18269), Proposition 3.1 (threshold signaling scheme); two-point case embedded in S signals

declarations.name: spi_two_point_pool_prob_mem
declarations.informal: The pooling probability lies in [0, 1].
declarations.statement:
lemma spi_two_point_pool_prob_mem (h l q T : ℝ) (hlh : l ≤ h) (hq0 : 0 ≤ q) (hq1 : q ≤ 1) :
    0 ≤ spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T ∧ spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T ≤ 1
declarations.source:
/-- The pooling probability lies in `[0, 1]` for a two-point reward with `l ≤ h` and `q ∈ [0, 1]`. -/
lemma spi_two_point_pool_prob_mem (h l q T : ℝ) (hlh : l ≤ h) (hq0 : 0 ≤ q) (hq1 : q ≤ 1) :
    0 ≤ spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T ∧ spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T ≤ 1 := by
  unfold spi_two_point_pool_prob
  split_ifs with h1 h2
  · norm_num
  · have hq1' : q < 1 := by
      by_contra hc; push Not at hc
      have e : q * h + (1 - q) * l = h := by rw [le_antisymm hq1 hc]; ring
      linarith
    have hTl : 0 < T - l := by nlinarith
    have h1q : 0 < 1 - q := by linarith
    constructor
    · apply div_nonneg <;> nlinarith
    · rw [div_le_one (by positivity)]; nlinarith
  · norm_num

declarations.name: spi_ite_null_signal
declarations.informal: A signal of probability m >= 0 whose posterior mean is below T contributes nothing to the acceptance probability.
declarations.statement:
lemma spi_ite_null_signal (T m c : ℝ) (hm : 0 ≤ m) (hc : c < T) :
    (if T * m ≤ m * c then m else 0) = 0
declarations.source:
/-- A signal of probability `m ≥ 0` whose posterior mean `c` is below `T` contributes nothing to the acceptance probability. -/
lemma spi_ite_null_signal (T m c : ℝ) (hm : 0 ≤ m) (hc : c < T) :
    (if T * m ≤ m * c then m else 0) = 0 := by
  split_ifs with h
  · nlinarith
  · rfl

declarations.name: spi_two_point_scheme_prob_eq
declarations.informal: Real-arithmetic part of the optimality of the two-point scheme: its two signals give acceptance probability exactly spi_two_point_max_prob.
declarations.statement:
lemma spi_two_point_scheme_prob_eq (h l q T : ℝ) (hlh : l ≤ h) (hq0 : 0 ≤ q) (hq1 : q ≤ 1) :
    (if T * (q * 1 + (1 - q) * spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T) ≤
        q * 1 * h + (1 - q) * spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T * l
      then q * 1 + (1 - q) * spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T else 0) +
    (if T * ((1 - q) * (1 - spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T)) ≤
        (1 - q) * (1 - spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T) * l
      then (1 - q) * (1 - spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T) else 0) =
    spi_two_point_max_prob h l q T
declarations.source:
/-- Real-arithmetic part of the optimality of `spi_two_point_scheme`: the accepted probability of its two signals (signal 0 with mass `q + (1-q) β`, signal 1 with mass `(1-q)(1-β)` and posterior mean `l`) equals `spi_two_point_max_prob`. -/
lemma spi_two_point_scheme_prob_eq (h l q T : ℝ) (hlh : l ≤ h) (hq0 : 0 ≤ q) (hq1 : q ≤ 1) :
    (if T * (q * 1 + (1 - q) * spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T) ≤
        q * 1 * h + (1 - q) * spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T * l
      then q * 1 + (1 - q) * spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T else 0) +
    (if T * ((1 - q) * (1 - spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T)) ≤
        (1 - q) * (1 - spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T) * l
      then (1 - q) * (1 - spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T) else 0) =
    spi_two_point_max_prob h l q T := by
  have hmem := spi_two_point_pool_prob_mem h l q T hlh hq0 hq1
  set β := spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T with hβ
  unfold spi_two_point_max_prob
  unfold spi_two_point_pool_prob at hβ
  by_cases h1 : T ≤ q * h + (1 - q) * l
  · rw [if_pos h1] at hβ ⊢
    rw [hβ, if_pos (by linarith)]
    simp
  · rw [if_neg h1] at hβ ⊢
    by_cases h2 : T ≤ h
    · rw [if_pos h2] at hβ ⊢
      have hq1' : q < 1 := by
        by_contra hc; push Not at hc
        have e : q * h + (1 - q) * l = h := by rw [le_antisymm hq1 hc]; ring
        linarith
      have hTl : 0 < T - l := by nlinarith
      have h1q : 0 < 1 - q := by linarith
      have hm0 : q * 1 + (1 - q) * β = q * (h - l) / (T - l) := by
        rw [hβ]; field_simp; ring
      have hv0 : q * 1 * h + (1 - q) * β * l = T * (q * (h - l) / (T - l)) := by
        rw [hβ]; field_simp; ring
      rw [hm0, hv0, if_pos le_rfl,
        spi_ite_null_signal T ((1 - q) * (1 - β)) l (mul_nonneg h1q.le (by linarith [hmem.2])) (by linarith)]
      ring
    · rw [if_neg h2] at hβ ⊢
      rw [hβ]
      simp only [mul_zero, zero_mul, add_zero, mul_one, sub_zero]
      rw [spi_ite_null_signal T q h hq0 (by linarith),
        spi_ite_null_signal T (1 - q) l (by linarith) (by linarith)]
      ring

declarations.name: spi_two_point_scheme_spec
declarations.informal: For S >= 2 the two-point scheme is a valid scheme and a player using it is accepted with probability exactly spi_two_point_max_prob.
declarations.statement:
open Finset in
lemma spi_two_point_scheme_spec {N S : ℕ} (hS : 2 ≤ S) (x w : Fin N → Fin 2 → ℝ) (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N)
    (h l q : ℝ) (hx0 : x i 0 = h) (hx1 : x i 1 = l) (hw0 : w i 0 = q) (hw1 : w i 1 = 1 - q)
    (hlh : l ≤ h) (hq0 : 0 ≤ q) (hq1 : q ≤ 1) :
    spi_is_scheme (spi_two_point_scheme S h l q T) ∧
      ∀ φ : Fin N → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ, φ i = spi_two_point_scheme S h l q T →
        spi_accept_prob x w φ T i = spi_two_point_max_prob h l q T
declarations.source:
open Finset in
/-- The scheme `spi_two_point_scheme` is a valid scheme for `S ≥ 2` signals, and a player using it gets accepted with probability exactly `spi_two_point_max_prob`. -/
lemma spi_two_point_scheme_spec {N S : ℕ} (hS : 2 ≤ S) (x w : Fin N → Fin 2 → ℝ) (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N)
    (h l q : ℝ) (hx0 : x i 0 = h) (hx1 : x i 1 = l) (hw0 : w i 0 = q) (hw1 : w i 1 = 1 - q)
    (hlh : l ≤ h) (hq0 : 0 ≤ q) (hq1 : q ≤ 1) :
    spi_is_scheme (spi_two_point_scheme S h l q T) ∧
      ∀ φ : Fin N → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ, φ i = spi_two_point_scheme S h l q T →
        spi_accept_prob x w φ T i = spi_two_point_max_prob h l q T := by
  have hmem := spi_two_point_pool_prob_mem h l q T hlh hq0 hq1
  let s0 : Fin S := ⟨0, by omega⟩
  let s1 : Fin S := ⟨1, by omega⟩
  have hs01 : s0 ≠ s1 := by simp [s0, s1, Fin.ext_iff]
  have hrest : ∀ s : Fin S, s ≠ s0 ∧ s ≠ s1 → ∀ k, spi_two_point_scheme S h l q T k s = 0 := by
    intro s ⟨h0, h1⟩ k
    have h0' : s.val ≠ 0 := fun e => h0 (Fin.ext e)
    have h1' : s.val ≠ 1 := fun e => h1 (Fin.ext e)
    simp [spi_two_point_scheme, h0', h1']
  have e00 : spi_two_point_scheme S h l q T 0 s0 = 1 := by simp [spi_two_point_scheme, s0]
  have e01 : spi_two_point_scheme S h l q T 0 s1 = 0 := by simp [spi_two_point_scheme, s1]
  have e10 : spi_two_point_scheme S h l q T 1 s0 = spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T := by
    simp [spi_two_point_scheme, s0]
  have e11 : spi_two_point_scheme S h l q T 1 s1 = 1 - spi_two_point_pool_prob h l q T := by
    simp [spi_two_point_scheme, s1]
  refine ⟨⟨fun k s => ?_, fun k => ?_⟩, fun φ hφ => ?_⟩
  · unfold spi_two_point_scheme; split_ifs <;> linarith [hmem.1, hmem.2]
  · rw [Fintype.sum_eq_add s0 s1 hs01 (fun s hs => hrest s hs k)]
    fin_cases k
    · simp only [Fin.zero_eta, e00, e01]; norm_num
    · simp only [Fin.mk_one, e10, e11]; ring
  · simp only [spi_accept_prob, spi_accepted]
    rw [Finset.sum_filter, Fintype.sum_eq_add s0 s1 hs01]
    · simp only [spi_signal_mass, spi_signal_value, Fin.sum_univ_two, hφ, hx0, hx1, hw0, hw1, e00, e01, e10, e11]
      have := spi_two_point_scheme_prob_eq h l q T hlh hq0 hq1
      simp only [mul_zero, zero_mul, zero_add] at this ⊢
      linarith [this]
    · intro s hs
      simp [spi_signal_mass, spi_signal_value, Fin.sum_univ_two, hφ, hrest s hs]
declarations.citation: Intrinsic Robustness of Prophet Inequality to Strategic Reward Signaling, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2409.18269), Proposition 3.1 (the threshold-signaling scheme attains the optimum); special case of two-point rewards, finite signal sets

declarations.name: spi_accept_congr
declarations.informal: Acceptance probability and accepted value of player i depend only on player i's own scheme.
declarations.statement:
lemma spi_accept_congr {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (φ φ' : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) (h : φ i = φ' i) :
    spi_accept_prob x w φ T i = spi_accept_prob x w φ' T i ∧
      spi_accept_value x w φ T i = spi_accept_value x w φ' T i
declarations.source:
/-- Acceptance probability and accepted value of player `i` only depend on player `i`'s own scheme. -/
lemma spi_accept_congr {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (φ φ' : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) (h : φ i = φ' i) :
    spi_accept_prob x w φ T i = spi_accept_prob x w φ' T i ∧
      spi_accept_value x w φ T i = spi_accept_value x w φ' T i := by
  simp only [spi_accept_prob, spi_accept_value, spi_accepted, spi_signal_mass, spi_signal_value, h]
  exact ⟨rfl, rfl⟩

declarations.name: spi_reach_prob_update
declarations.informal: A unilateral deviation of player i does not change the probability that the search reaches i.
declarations.statement:
open Finset in
lemma spi_reach_prob_update {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) (ψ : Fin K → Fin S → ℝ) :
    spi_reach_prob x w (Function.update φ i ψ) T i = spi_reach_prob x w φ T i
declarations.source:
open Finset in
/-- A unilateral deviation of player `i` does not change the probability that the search reaches `i`. -/
lemma spi_reach_prob_update {N K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin K → ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) (ψ : Fin K → Fin S → ℝ) :
    spi_reach_prob x w (Function.update φ i ψ) T i = spi_reach_prob x w φ T i := by
  unfold spi_reach_prob
  refine Finset.prod_congr rfl fun j hj => ?_
  have hji : j ≠ i := ne_of_lt (Finset.mem_filter.mp hj).2
  rw [(spi_accept_congr x w (Function.update φ i ψ) φ T j (Function.update_of_ne hji ψ φ)).1]

declarations.name: spi_reach_prob_nonneg
declarations.informal: Reach probabilities are nonnegative in a two-point instance under valid schemes.
declarations.statement:
open Finset in
lemma spi_reach_prob_nonneg {N S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin 2 → ℝ) (hinst : spi_is_two_point_instance x w)
    (φ : Fin N → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ) (hφ : ∀ i, spi_is_scheme (φ i)) (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) :
    0 ≤ spi_reach_prob x w φ T i
declarations.source:
open Finset in
/-- Reach probabilities are nonnegative in a two-point instance under valid schemes. -/
lemma spi_reach_prob_nonneg {N S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin 2 → ℝ) (hinst : spi_is_two_point_instance x w)
    (φ : Fin N → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ) (hφ : ∀ i, spi_is_scheme (φ i)) (T : ℝ) (i : Fin N) :
    0 ≤ spi_reach_prob x w φ T i := by
  unfold spi_reach_prob
  refine Finset.prod_nonneg fun j _ => ?_
  obtain ⟨-, -, h0, h1, hw1⟩ := hinst j
  have hw : ∀ k, 0 ≤ w j k := by
    intro k; fin_cases k
    · exact h0
    · simp only [Fin.mk_one, hw1]; linarith
  have := spi_accept_prob_mem_Icc x w φ T j hw (by rw [hw1]; ring) (hφ j)
  linarith [this.2]

declarations.name: spi_two_point_equilibrium_exists
declarations.informal: Existence of equilibrium (Proposition 3.1 for two-point rewards): for every static threshold and S >= 2 signals, all players using the two-point scheme is an equilibrium.
declarations.statement:
theorem spi_two_point_equilibrium_exists {N S : ℕ} (hS : 2 ≤ S) (x w : Fin N → Fin 2 → ℝ)
    (hinst : spi_is_two_point_instance x w) (T : ℝ) :
    spi_is_equilibrium x w T (fun i => spi_two_point_scheme S (x i 0) (x i 1) (w i 0) T)
declarations.source:
/-- Existence of equilibrium (Prop. 3.1 of arXiv:2409.18269, for two-point rewards): for every static threshold `T` and `S ≥ 2` signals, the profile in which every player uses `spi_two_point_scheme` is an equilibrium. -/
theorem spi_two_point_equilibrium_exists {N S : ℕ} (hS : 2 ≤ S) (x w : Fin N → Fin 2 → ℝ)
    (hinst : spi_is_two_point_instance x w) (T : ℝ) :
    spi_is_equilibrium x w T (fun i => spi_two_point_scheme S (x i 0) (x i 1) (w i 0) T) := by
  set φ : Fin N → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ := fun i => spi_two_point_scheme S (x i 0) (x i 1) (w i 0) T with hφdef
  have spec : ∀ i, spi_is_scheme (φ i) ∧ ∀ φ' : Fin N → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ, φ' i = φ i →
      spi_accept_prob x w φ' T i = spi_two_point_max_prob (x i 0) (x i 1) (w i 0) T := by
    intro i
    obtain ⟨-, hlh, h0, h1, hw1⟩ := hinst i
    exact spi_two_point_scheme_spec hS x w T i _ _ _ rfl rfl rfl hw1 hlh h0 h1
  refine ⟨fun i => (spec i).1, fun i ψ hψ => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨-, hlh, h0, h1, hw1⟩ := hinst i
  unfold spi_player_payoff
  rw [spi_reach_prob_update, (spec i).2 φ rfl]
  have hb := (spi_two_point_bound x w (Function.update φ i ψ) T i hlh h0 h1 hw1
    (by rw [Function.update_self]; exact hψ)).1
  exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hb (spi_reach_prob_nonneg x w hinst φ (fun j => (spec j).1) T i)

declarations.name: spi_two_point_equilibrium_pinned
declarations.informal: In every equilibrium of a two-point instance, every player reached with positive probability is accepted with probability spi_two_point_max_prob and contributes spi_two_point_max_value.
declarations.statement:
lemma spi_two_point_equilibrium_pinned {N S : ℕ} (hS : 2 ≤ S) (x w : Fin N → Fin 2 → ℝ)
    (hinst : spi_is_two_point_instance x w) (T : ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ)
    (heq : spi_is_equilibrium x w T φ) (i : Fin N) (hr : 0 < spi_reach_prob x w φ T i) :
    spi_accept_prob x w φ T i = spi_two_point_max_prob (x i 0) (x i 1) (w i 0) T ∧
      spi_accept_value x w φ T i = spi_two_point_max_value (x i 0) (x i 1) (w i 0) T
declarations.source:
/-- In every equilibrium of a two-point instance, every player that is reached with positive probability gets accepted with probability `spi_two_point_max_prob` and contributes accepted value `spi_two_point_max_value` (the equilibrium outcome of Prop. 3.1). -/
lemma spi_two_point_equilibrium_pinned {N S : ℕ} (hS : 2 ≤ S) (x w : Fin N → Fin 2 → ℝ)
    (hinst : spi_is_two_point_instance x w) (T : ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ)
    (heq : spi_is_equilibrium x w T φ) (i : Fin N) (hr : 0 < spi_reach_prob x w φ T i) :
    spi_accept_prob x w φ T i = spi_two_point_max_prob (x i 0) (x i 1) (w i 0) T ∧
      spi_accept_value x w φ T i = spi_two_point_max_value (x i 0) (x i 1) (w i 0) T := by
  obtain ⟨-, hlh, h0, h1, hw1⟩ := hinst i
  have hb := spi_two_point_bound x w φ T i hlh h0 h1 hw1 (heq.1 i)
  obtain ⟨hsch, hval⟩ := spi_two_point_scheme_spec hS x w T i _ _ _ rfl rfl rfl hw1 hlh h0 h1
  have hdev := heq.2 i _ hsch
  unfold spi_player_payoff at hdev
  rw [spi_reach_prob_update, hval _ (Function.update_self i _ φ)] at hdev
  have hge : spi_two_point_max_prob (x i 0) (x i 1) (w i 0) T ≤ spi_accept_prob x w φ T i :=
    le_of_mul_le_mul_left hdev hr
  exact ⟨le_antisymm hb.1 hge, hb.2 hge⟩

declarations.name: spi_two_point_above
declarations.informal: Above its high value (T > h) a two-point player is never accepted, whatever its scheme.
declarations.statement:
lemma spi_two_point_above {N S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin 2 → ℝ) (hinst : spi_is_two_point_instance x w)
    (T : ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ) {i : Fin N} (hφ : spi_is_scheme (φ i)) (hT : x i 0 < T) :
    spi_accept_prob x w φ T i = 0 ∧ spi_accept_value x w φ T i = 0
declarations.source:
/-- Above the high value (`T > h`) a two-point player is never accepted, whatever its scheme. -/
lemma spi_two_point_above {N S : ℕ} (x w : Fin N → Fin 2 → ℝ) (hinst : spi_is_two_point_instance x w)
    (T : ℝ) (φ : Fin N → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ) {i : Fin N} (hφ : spi_is_scheme (φ i)) (hT : x i 0 < T) :
    spi_accept_prob x w φ T i = 0 ∧ spi_accept_value x w φ T i = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨-, hlh, h0, h1, hw1⟩ := hinst i
  have hb := spi_two_point_bound x w φ T i hlh h0 h1 hw1 hφ
  have hw : ∀ k, 0 ≤ w i k := by
    intro k; fin_cases k
    · exact h0
    · simp only [Fin.mk_one, hw1]; linarith
  have hP := (spi_accept_prob_mem_Icc x w φ T i hw (by rw [hw1]; ring) hφ).1
  have hm : spi_two_point_max_prob (x i 0) (x i 1) (w i 0) T = 0 := by
    unfold spi_two_point_max_prob
    rw [if_neg (by nlinarith), if_neg (by linarith)]
  have hv : spi_two_point_max_value (x i 0) (x i 1) (w i 0) T = 0 := by
    unfold spi_two_point_max_value
    rw [if_neg (by nlinarith), if_neg (by linarith)]
  rw [hm] at hb

open Finset in
lemma spi_sum_fun_fin_four {β : Type*} [AddCommMonoid β] (f : (Fin 4 → Fin 2) → β) :
    ∑ k, f k = ∑ a : Fin 2, ∑ b : Fin 2, ∑ c : Fin 2, ∑ d : Fin 2, f ![a, b, c, d]
declarations.source:
open Finset in
/-- `E[max]` over four independent two-point rewards expands into a sum over the 16 value profiles. -/
lemma spi_sum_fun_fin_four {β : Type*} [AddCommMonoid β] (f : (Fin 4 → Fin 2) → β) :
    ∑ k, f k = ∑ a : Fin 2, ∑ b : Fin 2, ∑ c : Fin 2, ∑ d : Fin 2, f ![a, b, c, d] := by
  rw [← (Fin.consEquiv fun _ => Fin 2).sum_comp, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
  rw [← (Fin.consEquiv fun _ => Fin 2).sum_comp, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
  rw [← (Fin.consEquiv fun _ => Fin 2).sum_comp, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun c _ => ?_
  rw [← (Fin.consEquiv fun _ => Fin 2).sum_comp, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun d _ => ?_
  simp only [Fintype.sum_unique]
  congr 1

declarations.name: spi_reach_prob_fin_four
declarations.informal: For four players the reach probabilities are 1, 1-P0, (1-P0)(1-P1) and (1-P0)(1-P1)(1-P2).
declarations.statement:
open Finset in
lemma spi_reach_prob_fin_four {K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin 4 → Fin K → ℝ) (φ : Fin 4 → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ) (T : ℝ) :
    spi_reach_prob x w φ T 0 = 1 ∧
    spi_reach_prob x w φ T 1 = 1 - spi_accept_prob x w φ T 0 ∧
    spi_reach_prob x w φ T 2 = (1 - spi_accept_prob x w φ T 0) * (1 - spi_accept_prob x w φ T 1) ∧
    spi_reach_prob x w φ T 3 = (1 - spi_accept_prob x w φ T 0) * (1 - spi_accept_prob x w φ T 1) *
      (1 - spi_accept_prob x w φ T 2)

/-- For four players, the reach probabilities are `1`, `1 - P₀`, `(1 - P₀)(1 - P₁)` and `(1 - P₀)(1 - P₁)(1 - P₂)`. -/
lemma spi_reach_prob_fin_four {K S : ℕ} (x w : Fin 4 → Fin K → ℝ) (φ : Fin 4 → Fin K → Fin S → ℝ) (T : ℝ) :
    spi_reach_prob x w φ T 0 = 1 ∧
    spi_reach_prob x w φ T 1 = 1 - spi_accept_prob x w φ T 0 ∧
    spi_reach_prob x w φ T 2 = (1 - spi_accept_prob x w φ T 0) * (1 - spi_accept_prob x w φ T 1) ∧
    spi_reach_prob x w φ T 3 = (1 - spi_accept_prob x w φ T 0) * (1 - spi_accept_prob x w φ T 1) *
      (1 - spi_accept_prob x w φ T 2) := by
  simp [spi_reach_prob, Finset.prod_filter, Fin.prod_univ_four]

declarations.name: spx_payoff_mid
declarations.informal: For 24/5 < T <= 9, every equilibrium of the four-player instance gives the searcher T p1 + (1-p1)(10/3 + (1-p2) 8/5) with p1 = (3/5)/(T-3), p2 = (10/3)/T.
declarations.statement:
open Finset in
lemma spx_payoff_mid {S : ℕ} (hS : 2 ≤ S) (T : ℝ) (φ : Fin 4 → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ)
    (heq : spi_is_equilibrium spx_x spx_w T φ) (hT1 : 24 / 5 < T) (hT2 : T ≤ 9) :
    spi_searcher_payoff spx_x spx_w φ T =
      T * ((3 / 5) / (T - 3)) + (1 - (3 / 5) / (T - 3)) * (10 / 3 + (1 - (10 / 3) / T) * (8 / 5))
declarations.source:
open Finset in
/-- In any equilibrium with threshold `24/5 < T ≤ 9`, the searcher's payoff in the four-player instance is `T p₁ + (1 - p₁)(10/3 + (1 - p₂) 8/5)` with `p₁ = (3/5)/(T - 3)` and `p₂ = (10/3)/T`. -/
lemma spx_payoff_mid {S : ℕ} (hS : 2 ≤ S) (T : ℝ) (φ : Fin 4 → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ)
    (heq : spi_is_equilibrium spx_x spx_w T φ) (hT1 : 24 / 5 < T) (hT2 : T ≤ 9) :
    spi_searcher_payoff spx_x spx_w φ T =
      T * ((3 / 5) / (T - 3)) + (1 - (3 / 5) / (T - 3)) * (10 / 3 + (1 - (10 / 3) / T) * (8 / 5)) := by
  obtain ⟨r0, r1, r2, r3⟩ := spi_reach_prob_fin_four spx_x spx_w φ T
  have a0 := spi_two_point_above spx_x spx_w spx_instance T φ (i := 0) (heq.1 0)
    (by simp [spx_x]; linarith)
  have p1 := spi_two_point_equilibrium_pinned hS spx_x spx_w spx_instance T φ heq 1
    (by rw [r1, a0.1]; norm_num)
  have hT3 : 0 < T - 3 := by linarith
  obtain ⟨x00, x01, w00, x10, x11, w10, x20, x21, w20, x30, x31, w30⟩ := spx_vals
  have mid1 := spi_two_point_max_mid 9 3 (1 / 10) T (by norm_num; linarith) hT2
  have hm1 : spi_two_point_max_prob (spx_x 1 0) (spx_x 1 1) (spx_w 1 0) T = (3 / 5) / (T - 3) := by
    rw [x10, x11, w10, mid1.1]; ring
  have hv1 : spi_two_point_max_value (spx_x 1 0) (spx_x 1 1) (spx_w 1 0) T = T * ((3 / 5) / (T - 3)) := by
    rw [x10, x11, w10, mid1.2]; ring
  have hP1 : (3 / 5) / (T - 3) < 1 := by rw [div_lt_one hT3]; linarith
  have p2 := spi_two_point_equilibrium_pinned hS spx_x spx_w spx_instance T φ heq 2
    (by rw [r2, a0.1, p1.1, hm1]; nlinarith)
  have mid2 := spi_two_point_max_mid 1000 0 (1 / 300) T (by norm_num; linarith) (by linarith)
  have hm2 : spi_two_point_max_prob (spx_x 2 0) (spx_x 2 1) (spx_w 2 0) T = (10 / 3) / T := by
    rw [x20, x21, w20, mid2.1]; ring
  have hv2 : spi_two_point_max_value (spx_x 2 0) (spx_x 2 1) (spx_w 2 0) T = 10 / 3 := by
    rw [x20, x21, w20, mid2.2]; have hT0' : T ≠ 0 := by linarith
    field_simp; try ring
  have hP2 : (10 / 3) / T < 1 := by rw [div_lt_one (by linarith)]; linarith
  have p3 := spi_two_point_equilibrium_pinned hS spx_x spx_w spx_instance T φ heq 3
    (by rw [r3, a0.1, p1.1, p2.1, hm1, hm2]; apply mul_pos <;> nlinarith)
  have mid3 := spi_two_point_max_mid 40 0 (1 / 25) T (by norm_num; linarith) (by linarith)
  have hv3 : spi_two_point_max_value (spx_x 3 0) (spx_x 3 1) (spx_w 3 0) T = 8 / 5 := by
    rw [x30, x31, w30, mid3.2]; have hT0' : T ≠ 0 := by linarith
    field_simp; try ring
  simp only [spi_searcher_payoff, Fin.sum_univ_four, r0, r1, r2, r3, a0.1, a0.2, p1.1, p1.2, p2.1, p2.2,
    p3.2, hm1, hv1, hm2, hv2, hv3]
  ring

declarations.name: spx_searcher_payoff_le
declarations.informal: In the four-player instance, for every static threshold T, every S >= 2 and every equilibrium, the searcher's expected payoff is at most 721/150.
declarations.statement:
open Finset in
theorem spx_searcher_payoff_le {S : ℕ} (hS : 2 ≤ S) (T : ℝ) (φ : Fin 4 → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ)
    (heq : spi_is_equilibrium spx_x spx_w T φ) :
    spi_searcher_payoff spx_x spx_w φ T ≤ 721 / 150
declarations.source:
open Finset in
/-- In the four-player instance, for every static threshold `T`, every number `S ≥ 2` of signals and every equilibrium of the players' signaling game, the searcher's expected payoff is at most `721/150`. -/
theorem spx_searcher_payoff_le {S : ℕ} (hS : 2 ≤ S) (T : ℝ) (φ : Fin 4 → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ)
    (heq : spi_is_equilibrium spx_x spx_w T φ) :
    spi_searcher_payoff spx_x spx_w φ T ≤ 721 / 150 := by
  obtain ⟨r0, r1, r2, r3⟩ := spi_reach_prob_fin_four spx_x spx_w φ T
  have p0 := spi_two_point_equilibrium_pinned hS spx_x spx_w spx_instance T φ heq 0 (by rw [r0]; norm_num)
  obtain ⟨x00, x01, w00, x10, x11, w10, x20, x21, w20, x30, x31, w30⟩ := spx_vals
  by_cases hA : T ≤ 24 / 5
  · have low0 := spi_two_point_max_low (24 / 5) 0 1 T (by norm_num; linarith)
    have hm0 : spi_two_point_max_prob (spx_x 0 0) (spx_x 0 1) (spx_w 0 0) T = 1 := by
      rw [x00, x01, w00, low0.1]
    have hv0 : spi_two_point_max_value (spx_x 0 0) (spx_x 0 1) (spx_w 0 0) T = 24 / 5 := by
      rw [x00, x01, w00, low0.2]; norm_num
    simp only [spi_searcher_payoff, Fin.sum_univ_four, r0, r1, r2, r3, p0.1, p0.2, hm0, hv0]
    norm_num
  push Not at hA
  by_cases hB : T ≤ 9
  · rw [spx_payoff_mid hS T φ heq hA hB]
    have hT3 : 0 < T - 3 := by linarith
    have hT0 : 0 < T := by linarith
    have key : T * ((3 / 5) / (T - 3)) + (1 - (3 / 5) / (T - 3)) * (10 / 3 + (1 - (10 / 3) / T) * (8 / 5)) =
        721 / 150 - (9 - T) * (109 * T - 320) / (150 * T * (T - 3)) := by
      field_simp; ring
    have hnn : 0 ≤ (9 - T) * (109 * T - 320) / (150 * T * (T - 3)) := by
      apply div_nonneg
      · apply mul_nonneg <;> linarith
      · positivity
    linarith
  push Not at hB
  have a0 := spi_two_point_above spx_x spx_w spx_instance T φ (i := 0) (heq.1 0) (by simp [spx_x]; linarith)
  have a1 := spi_two_point_above spx_x spx_w spx_instance T φ (i := 1) (heq.1 1) (by simp [spx_x]; linarith)
  by_cases hC : T ≤ 1000
  · have p2 := spi_two_point_equilibrium_pinned hS spx_x spx_w spx_instance T φ heq 2
      (by rw [r2, a0.1, a1.1]; norm_num)
    have mid2 := spi_two_point_max_mid 1000 0 (1 / 300) T (by norm_num; linarith) hC
    have hm2 : spi_two_point_max_prob (spx_x 2 0) (spx_x 2 1) (spx_w 2 0) T = (10 / 3) / T := by
      rw [x20, x21, w20, mid2.1]; ring
    have hv2 : spi_two_point_max_value (spx_x 2 0) (spx_x 2 1) (spx_w 2 0) T = 10 / 3 := by
      have hT0' : T ≠ 0 := by linarith
      rw [x20, x21, w20, mid2.2]; field_simp; try ring
    have hT0 : 0 < T := by linarith
    by_cases hD : T ≤ 40
    · have p3 := spi_two_point_equilibrium_pinned hS spx_x spx_w spx_instance T φ heq 3
        (by
          rw [r3, a0.1, a1.1, p2.1, hm2]
          have hP2 : (10 / 3) / T < 1 := by rw [div_lt_one hT0]; linarith
          simp only [sub_zero, one_mul]; linarith)
      have mid3 := spi_two_point_max_mid 40 0 (1 / 25) T (by norm_num; linarith) hD
      have hv3 : spi_two_point_max_value (spx_x 3 0) (spx_x 3 1) (spx_w 3 0) T = 8 / 5 := by
        have hT0' : T ≠ 0 := by linarith
        rw [x30, x31, w30, mid3.2]; field_simp; try ring
      simp only [spi_searcher_payoff, Fin.sum_univ_four, r0, r1, r2, r3, a0.1, a0.2, a1.1, a1.2, p2.1, p2.2,
        p3.2, hm2, hv2, hv3]
      have : (10 / 3) / T ≥ 1 / 12 := by rw [ge_iff_le, le_div_iff₀ hT0]; linarith
      nlinarith
    · push Not at hD
      have a3 := spi_two_point_above spx_x spx_w spx_instance T φ (i := 3) (heq.1 3) (by simp [spx_x]; linarith)
      simp only [spi_searcher_payoff, Fin.sum_univ_four, r0, r1, r2, r3, a0.1, a0.2, a1.1, a1.2, p2.1, p2.2,
        a3.2, hv2]
      norm_num
  · push Not at hC
    have a2 := spi_two_point_above spx_x spx_w spx_instance T φ (i := 2) (heq.1 2) (by simp [spx_x]; linarith)
    have a3 := spi_two_point_above spx_x spx_w spx_instance T φ (i := 3) (heq.1 3) (by simp [spx_x]; linarith)
    simp only [spi_searcher_payoff, Fin.sum_univ_four, r0, r1, r2, r3, a0.2, a1.2, a2.2, a3.2]
    norm_num

declarations.name: spx_searcher_payoff_at_nine

theorem spx_searcher_payoff_at_nine {S : ℕ} (hS : 2 ≤ S) (φ : Fin 4 → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ)
    (heq : spi_is_equilibrium spx_x spx_w 9 φ) :
    spi_searcher_payoff spx_x spx_w φ 9 = 721 / 150
declarations.source:
/-- The bound `721/150` is attained: with threshold `T = 9`, every equilibrium gives the searcher exactly `721/150`. -/
theorem spx_searcher_payoff_at_nine {S : ℕ} (hS : 2 ≤ S) (φ : Fin 4 → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ)
    (heq : spi_is_equilibrium spx_x spx_w 9 φ) :
    spi_searcher_payoff spx_x spx_w φ 9 = 721 / 150 := by
  rw [spx_payoff_mid hS 9 φ heq (by norm_num) le_rfl]
  norm_num

declarations.name: strategic_prophet_no_half_robust_static_threshold
declarations.informal: Negative answer to the open question of arXiv:2409.18269: in a four-player two-point instance, equilibria exist for every static threshold, every equilibrium gives the searcher at most 721/150 < OPT/2 with OPT = 155039/15625, and T = 9 attains 721/150 = (450625/930234) OPT ~ 0.4844 OPT; so no static threshold is 1/2-robust.
declarations.statement:
theorem strategic_prophet_no_half_robust_static_threshold :
    spi_is_two_point_instance spx_x spx_w ∧
    @spi_prophet_value 3 2 spx_x spx_w = 155039 / 15625 ∧
    (∀ S, 2 ≤ S → ∀ T : ℝ, ∃ φ : Fin 4 → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ, spi_is_equilibrium spx_x spx_w T φ) ∧
    (∀ S, 2 ≤ S → ∀ (T : ℝ) (φ : Fin 4 → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ), spi_is_equilibrium spx_x spx_w T φ →
      spi_searcher_payoff spx_x spx_w φ T ≤ 721 / 150 ∧
      spi_searcher_payoff spx_x spx_w φ T < @spi_prophet_value 3 2 spx_x spx_w / 2) ∧
    (∀ S, 2 ≤ S → ∀ φ : Fin 4 → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ, spi_is_equilibrium spx_x spx_w 9 φ →
      spi_searcher_payoff spx_x spx_w φ 9 = 450625 / 930234 * @spi_prophet_value 3 2 spx_x spx_w)
declarations.source:
/-- Negative answer to the open question of arXiv:2409.18269 (NeurIPS 2024, Remark 4.1 and Sec. 6) on whether a static threshold stopping policy can be 1/2-robust under strategic reward signaling: in a four-player two-point instance, for every threshold `T` equilibria exist, and in every equilibrium the searcher gets at most `721/150`, while `OPT/2 = 155039/31250 > 721/150`; the best static threshold (`T = 9`) attains exactly `721/150 = (450625/930234) · OPT ≈ 0.4844 · OPT`. -/
theorem strategic_prophet_no_half_robust_static_threshold :
    spi_is_two_point_instance spx_x spx_w ∧
    @spi_prophet_value 3 2 spx_x spx_w = 155039 / 15625 ∧
    (∀ S, 2 ≤ S → ∀ T : ℝ, ∃ φ : Fin 4 → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ, spi_is_equilibrium spx_x spx_w T φ) ∧
    (∀ S, 2 ≤ S → ∀ (T : ℝ) (φ : Fin 4 → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ), spi_is_equilibrium spx_x spx_w T φ →
      spi_searcher_payoff spx_x spx_w φ T ≤ 721 / 150 ∧
      spi_searcher_payoff spx_x spx_w φ T < @spi_prophet_value 3 2 spx_x spx_w / 2) ∧
    (∀ S, 2 ≤ S → ∀ φ : Fin 4 → Fin 2 → Fin S → ℝ, spi_is_equilibrium spx_x spx_w 9 φ →
      spi_searcher_payoff spx_x spx_w φ 9 = 450625 / 930234 * @spi_prophet_value 3 2 spx_x spx_w) := by
  refine ⟨spx_instance, spx_prophet_value, fun S hS T => ⟨_, spi_two_point_equilibrium_exists hS _ _ spx_instance T⟩,
    fun S hS T φ heq => ⟨spx_searcher_payoff_le hS T φ heq, ?_⟩, fun S hS φ heq => ?_⟩
  · rw [spx_prophet_value]; linarith [spx_searcher_payoff_le hS T φ heq]
  · rw [spx_searcher_payoff_at_nine hS φ heq, spx_prophet_value]; norm_num

declarations.name: slice_rank_floor
declarations.informal: The slice-rank lower bound floor G(k) for the GF(2^k) multiplication oracle is the sum over i from 0 to 3k-1 of ceil((2k+2)/2^i).
declarations.statement: def slice_rank_floor (k : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.source:
/-- The Griesmer slice-rank floor G(k) for the GF(2^k) multiplication oracle. -/
def slice_rank_floor (k : ℕ) : ℕ := ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (3 * k), (2 * k + 2 + 2 ^ i - 1) / 2 ^ i
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.01024, Proposition 59
declarations.reading: `slice_rank_floor` is defined as a function from `ℕ` to `ℕ` that maps each natural number `k` to the sum over `i ∈ Finset.range (3 * k)` (that is, for `i` from `0` to `3 * k - 1`) of `(2 * k + 2 + 2 ^ i - 1) / 2 ^ i`, where `/` is truncated natural number division (which computes ⌈(2k + 2) / 2^i⌉).

declarations.name: gf8_mult_coeff
declarations.informal: The structure constants for multiplication in GF(8) with respect to the basis {1, alpha, alpha^2} with irreducible polynomial alpha^3 + alpha + 1.
declarations.statement: def gf8_mult_coeff (q r l : Fin 3) : ZMod 2
declarations.source:
/-- Multiplication structure constants of GF(8) in the polynomial basis with alpha^3 = alpha + 1. -/
def gf8_mult_coeff (q r l : Fin 3) : ZMod 2 := match q.val + r.val, l.val with | 0, 0 => 1 | 1, 1 => 1 | 2, 2 => 1 | 3, 0 => 1 | 3, 1 => 1 | 4, 1 => 1 | 4, 2 => 1 | _, _ => 0
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.01024, Proposition 55
declarations.reading:
A definition of a function `gf8_mult_coeff` mapping three elements `q`, `r`, and `l` of `Fin 3` to `ZMod 2`. Its value is determined by the natural number sum `q.val + r.val` and the natural number `l.val`:
- It evaluates to `1` if `(q.val + r.val, l.val)` is equal to `(0, 0)`, `(1, 1)`, `(2, 2)`, `(3, 0)`, `(3, 1)`, `(4, 1)`, or `(4, 2)`.
- It evaluates to `0` for all other pairs `(q.val + r.val, l.val)`.

declarations.name: Matrix3Triad
declarations.informal: Given a type R, a Matrix3Triad R is a structure consisting of three 3-by-3 matrices with entries in R, labeled u, v, and w.
declarations.statement: structure Matrix3Triad (R : Type*)
declarations.source:
/-- A triad product for 3x3 matrices over a type R. -/
structure Matrix3Triad (R : Type*) where
  u : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) R
  v : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) R
  w : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) R
declarations.reading: A structure `Matrix3Triad R`, parameterized by a type `R`, bundling three $3 \times 3$ matrices over `R`: fields `u`, `v`, and `w`, each of type `Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) R`.

declarations.name: eval_matrix3_triad
declarations.informal: Given a commutative semiring R, a triad t of type Matrix3Triad R, and 3x3 matrices A and B over R, eval_matrix3_triad t A B is the scalar multiple of t.w by the product of the sum of t.u i j * A i j and the sum of t.v i j * B i j over all i and j in Fin 3.
declarations.statement: def eval_matrix3_triad {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (t : Matrix3Triad R) (A B : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) R) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) R
declarations.source:
/-- Bilinear evaluation of a 3x3 triad on input matrices A and B. -/
def eval_matrix3_triad {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (t : Matrix3Triad R) (A B : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) R) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) R :=
  let sA := ∑ i : Fin 3, ∑ j : Fin 3, t.u i j * A i j
  let sB := ∑ i : Fin 3, ∑ j : Fin 3, t.v i j * B i j
  (sA * sB) • t.w
declarations.reading: `eval_matrix3_triad` is a definition that takes a commutative semiring `R`, a triad `t` of $3 \times 3$ matrices `t.u`, `t.v`, `t.w` over `R`, and two $3 \times 3$ matrices `A` and `B` over `R`, and produces the $3 \times 3$ matrix over `R` obtained by scalar multiplying `t.w` by the product of two scalars: the sum over all entries $(i, j) \in \{0, 1, 2\}^2$ of $(t.u)_{i,j} \cdot A_{i,j}$, and the sum over all entries $(i, j) \in \{0, 1, 2\}^2$ of $(t.v)_{i,j} \cdot B_{i,j}$.

declarations.name: eval_matrix3_decomposition
declarations.informal: Given a commutative semiring R, a list L of Matrix3Triad R, and 3x3 matrices A and B over R, eval_matrix3_decomposition L A B is the sum of eval_matrix3_triad t A B for t in L.
declarations.statement: def eval_matrix3_decomposition {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (L : List (Matrix3Triad R)) (A B : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) R) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) R
declarations.reading: A definition that, given a commutative semiring `R`, a list `L` of `Matrix3Triad R` structures, and two 3×3 matrices `A` and `B` over `R`, computes a 3×3 matrix over `R` by applying `eval_matrix3_triad` to each triad in `L` with matrices `A` and `B`, and summing the resulting list of matrices.

declarations.name: is_valid_matrix3_decomposition
declarations.informal: Given a commutative semiring R and a list L of Matrix3Triad R, is_valid_matrix3_decomposition L asserts that for all 3x3 matrices A and B over R, eval_matrix3_decomposition L A B equals A * B.
declarations.statement: def is_valid_matrix3_decomposition {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (L : List (Matrix3Triad R)) : Prop
declarations.reading: Given a commutative semiring `R` and a list `L` of `Matrix3Triad R` (triads of 3×3 matrices `u`, `v`, `w` over `R`), `is_valid_matrix3_decomposition L` asserts that for all 3×3 matrices `A` and `B` over `R`, the evaluated decomposition `eval_matrix3_decomposition L A B` equals the matrix product `A * B`. Here, the evaluation on `A` and `B` sums over each triad `t` in `L` the matrix `(sA * sB) • t.w`, where `sA` is the entrywise product sum `∑ i j, t.u i j * A i j` and `sB` is `∑ i j, t.v i j * B i j`.

declarations.name: matrix3_tensor_rank_le
declarations.informal: For a commutative semiring R and a natural number r, matrix3_tensor_rank_le R r asserts that there exists a list L of elements of Matrix3Triad R with length at most r such that is_valid_matrix3_decomposition L holds.
declarations.statement: def matrix3_tensor_rank_le (R : Type*) [CommSemiring R] (r : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.reading: Given a commutative semiring $R$ and a natural number $r$, `matrix3_tensor_rank_le R r` asserts that there exists a list $L$ of $3 \times 3$ matrix triads over $R$ of length at most $r$ such that $L$ is a valid decomposition of $3 \times 3$ matrix multiplication over $R$ (that is, evaluating the decomposition on any pair of $3 \times 3$ matrices $A$ and $B$ yields their matrix product $A * B$).

declarations.name: matrix3_tensor_rank_ge
declarations.informal: For a commutative semiring R and a natural number r, matrix3_tensor_rank_ge R r asserts that for every list L of elements of Matrix3Triad R, if is_valid_matrix3_decomposition L holds, then r is less than or equal to the length of L.
declarations.statement: def matrix3_tensor_rank_ge (R : Type*) [CommSemiring R] (r : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.reading: For a commutative semiring `R` and a natural number `r`, the proposition asserts that every list `L` of triads `(u, v, w)` of 3×3 matrices over `R` that forms a valid bilinear decomposition of 3×3 matrix multiplication (that is, for all 3×3 matrices `A` and `B` over `R`, the sum over triads in `L` of `(∑_{i,j} u_{ij} A_{ij}) * (∑_{i,j} v_{ij} B_{ij}) • w` equals the matrix product `A * B`) has length at least `r`.

declarations.name: matrix3_tensor_rank_exactly
declarations.informal: For a commutative semiring R and a natural number r, matrix3_tensor_rank_exactly R r is the conjunction of matrix3_tensor_rank_le R r and matrix3_tensor_rank_ge R r.
declarations.statement: def matrix3_tensor_rank_exactly (R : Type*) [CommSemiring R] (r : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.reading:
Given a commutative semiring `R` and a natural number `r`, the proposition asserts the conjunction of two conditions:
1. There exists a list `L` of `Matrix3Triad R` such that `L.length ≤ r` and `L` is a valid decomposition of $3 \times 3$ matrix multiplication (meaning for all $3 \times 3$ matrices $A$ and $B$ over `R`, evaluating the decomposition `L` on $A$ and $B$ by summing `eval_matrix3_triad t A B` over all triads $t \in L$ yields $A * B$).
2. For every list `L` of `Matrix3Triad R`, if `L` is a valid decomposition of $3 \times 3$ matrix multiplication, then `r ≤ L.length`.

Equivalently, $r$ is the minimum length among all valid triad decompositions of $3 \times 3$ matrix multiplication over $R$ (i.e., the tensor rank / bilinear complexity of $3 \times 3$ matrix multiplication over $R$ is exactly $r$).

declarations.name: is_parity_repr
declarations.informal: A finite set S of nonempty parities on n qubits is a parity representation of a syndrome s if the moment of S at every non-empty subset A of qubits of cardinality at most 3 matches s(A) modulo 2.
declarations.statement: def is_parity_repr {n : ℕ} (S : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (s : Finset (Fin n) → ZMod 2) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- A set S of nonempty parities on n qubits represents a syndrome s if for all subsets A of size 1, 2, or 3, the number of parities containing A has parity matching s A. -/
def is_parity_repr {n : ℕ} (S : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (s : Finset (Fin n) → ZMod 2) : Prop := (∀ y ∈ S, y.Nonempty) ∧
  (∀ A : Finset (Fin n), 1 ≤ A.card ∧ A.card ≤ 3 →
    ((S.filter (fun y => A ⊆ y)).card : ZMod 2) = s A)
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.01024, Definition 20 and Fact 21
declarations.reading:
Given a natural number $n$, a family of subsets $S$ of $\mathrm{Fin}(n)$ (i.e., a `Finset (Finset (Fin n))`), and a function $s : \mathrm{Finset}(\mathrm{Fin}(n)) \to \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, the definition `is_parity_repr S s` asserts that:

1. Every element $y \in S$ is non-empty (`y.Nonempty`).
2. For every subset $A \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}(n)$ whose cardinality satisfies $1 \le |A| \le 3$, the number of sets $y \in S$ that contain $A$ ($A \subseteq y$), reduced modulo 2 (as an element of $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$), equals $s(A)$.

declarations.name: line_cubic_form
declarations.informal: The line cubic form f_n on (ZMod 2)^n is the sum over i from 0 to n-3 of the product of adjacent triples x_i * x_{i+1} * x_{i+2}.
declarations.statement: def line_cubic_form (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → ZMod 2) : ZMod 2
declarations.source:
/-- The line cubic form f_n(x) = ∑ x_i x_{i+1} x_{i+2} on (ZMod 2)^n. -/
def line_cubic_form (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → ZMod 2) : ZMod 2 := ∑ i : Fin (n - 2),
    have h0 : i.val < n := by omega
    have h1 : i.val + 1 < n := by omega
    have h2 : i.val + 2 < n := by omega
    x ⟨i.val, h0⟩ * x ⟨i.val + 1, h1⟩ * x ⟨i.val + 2, h2⟩
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.01024, Proposition 65
declarations.reading: Definition of `line_cubic_form`: Given a natural number `n` and a function `x : Fin n → ZMod 2`, `line_cubic_form n x` is the element of `ZMod 2` defined as the sum over all `i : Fin (n - 2)` of the product `x ⟨i.val, _⟩ * x ⟨i.val + 1, _⟩ * x ⟨i.val + 2, _⟩`. Concretely, for `n ≥ 3`, this is ∑_{i=0}^{n-3} x_i * x_{i+1} * x_{i+2} in ZMod 2, and for `n < 3`, it is the empty sum (0).

declarations.name: line_syndrome
declarations.informal: The syndrome of the line cubic form assigns 1 to adjacent triples {i, i+1, i+2} and 0 to all other subsets of Fin n.
declarations.statement: def line_syndrome (n : ℕ) (A : Finset (Fin n)) : ZMod 2
declarations.source:
/-- The syndrome of the line cubic form, supported on adjacent index triples. -/
def line_syndrome (n : ℕ) (A : Finset (Fin n)) : ZMod 2 := if ∃ i : Fin (n - 2), A = {⟨i.val, by omega⟩, ⟨i.val + 1, by omega⟩, ⟨i.val + 2, by omega⟩} then 1 else 0
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.01024, Definition 20 and Proposition 65
declarations.reading: Given a natural number $n$ and a finite subset $A$ of $\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, $\mathrm{line\_syndrome}(n, A)$ is defined to be the element of $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ that is $1$ if there exists an index $i \in \mathrm{Fin}(n - 2)$ such that $A$ is the three-element set $\{i, i + 1, i + 2\}$ (cast into $\mathrm{Fin}(n)$), and $0$ otherwise.

declarations.name: eval_matrix3_decomposition_apply
declarations.informal: Entry (i, j) of the evaluation of a list of 3x3 triads on A and B is the sum, over the triads, of (sum of u_kl A_kl) times (sum of v_kl B_kl) times w_ij.
declarations.statement: theorem eval_matrix3_decomposition_apply {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (L : List (Matrix3Triad R)) (A B : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) R) (i j : Fin 3) : eval_matrix3_decomposition L A B i j = (L.map fun t => (∑ k : Fin 3, ∑ l : Fin 3, t.u k l * A k l) * (∑ k : Fin 3, ∑ l : Fin 3, t.v k l * B k l) * t.w i j).sum
declarations.source:
theorem eval_matrix3_decomposition_apply {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (L : List (Matrix3Triad R)) (A B : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) R) (i j : Fin 3) : eval_matrix3_decomposition L A B i j = (L.map fun t => (∑ k : Fin 3, ∑ l : Fin 3, t.u k l * A k l) * (∑ k : Fin 3, ∑ l : Fin 3, t.v k l * B k l) * t.w i j).sum := by
  induction L with
  | nil => simp [eval_matrix3_decomposition]
  | cons t L ih =>
    simp only [eval_matrix3_decomposition, List.map_cons, List.sum_cons, Matrix.add_apply] at ih ⊢
    rw [ih]
    simp [eval_matrix3_triad, smul_eq_mul]
declarations.citation: step towards the 3x3 matrix-multiplication rank statements (arXiv:2610.01639): entrywise evaluation of a triad decomposition

explanation.summary: The theorem is proved by structural induction on the list L of triads. The base case for the empty list is immediate since both sides reduce to zero. In the inductive step, the decomposition and the scalar sum are split into the contribution of the head triad and the sum over the tail list. Applying the induction hypothesis cancels the tail terms, and unfolding the definition of a single triad evaluation shows that its (i, j) entry matches the required scalar product with w_ij.

steps.claim: The identity holds for the empty list L = [].
steps.explanation: We proceed by structural induction on the list L. In the base case where L is empty, the matrix decomposition evaluates to the zero matrix (with (i, j) entry 0), and the sum over the empty list on the right-hand side is also 0.
steps.code:
induction L with
  | nil => simp [eval_matrix3_decomposition]

steps.claim: Assuming the identity holds for L, the goal for the non-empty list t :: L reduces to matching the head triad t.
steps.explanation: Unfolding eval_matrix3_decomposition and applying List.map_cons, List.sum_cons, and Matrix.add_apply separates both the matrix evaluation at entry (i, j) and the scalar sum into a head term corresponding to t and a tail sum corresponding to L. Rewriting with the induction hypothesis ih equates the tail terms, leaving only the head triad terms to be reconciled.
steps.code:
| cons t L ih =>
    simp only [eval_matrix3_decomposition, List.map_cons, List.sum_cons, Matrix.add_apply] at ih ⊢
    rw [ih]

steps.claim: The (i, j) entry of eval_matrix3_triad t A B matches the head term (∑ k l, t.u k l * A k l) * (∑ k l, t.v k l * B k l) * t.w i j, completing the proof.
steps.explanation: By definition of eval_matrix3_triad, the triad evaluates to the product of the two Frobenius inner products scaled by the matrix t.w. Evaluating at index (i, j) converts scalar multiplication to ring multiplication via smul_eq_mul, which identically matches the remaining goal.
steps.code: simp [eval_matrix3_triad, smul_eq_mul]

glossary.eval_matrix3_decomposition: The evaluation of a list of triads on matrices A and B, defined as the sum over the list of each triad evaluated on A and B: (L.map (fun t => eval_matrix3_triad t A B)).sum.
glossary.List.map_cons: Mapping a function over a non-empty list applies the function to the head element and prepends the result to the mapped tail: List.map f (x :: xs) = f x :: List.map f xs.
glossary.List.sum_cons: The sum of a non-empty list is the head element added to the sum of the tail: (x :: xs).sum = x + xs.sum.
glossary.Matrix.add_apply: Entry (i, j) of the sum of two matrices is the sum of their (i, j) entries: (M + N) i j = M i j + N i j.
glossary.eval_matrix3_triad: The evaluation of a triad t = (u, v, w) on matrices A and B, defined as the scalar product (∑ u_kl A_kl) * (∑ v_kl B_kl) multiplying the matrix w.
glossary.smul_eq_mul: Scalar multiplication of ring elements agrees with multiplication in the ring: a • b = a * b.

declarations.name: matrix3_tensor_rank_le_23_of_comm_ring
declarations.informal: Over every commutative ring R, 3x3 matrix multiplication has a valid bilinear decomposition with 23 products (the classical 23-multiplication algorithm with integer coefficients 0, 1, -1); hence its rank over R is at most 23.
declarations.statement: theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_le_23_of_comm_ring (R : Type*) [CommRing R] : matrix3_tensor_rank_le R 23
declarations.citation: A noncommutative algorithm for multiplying matrices using 23 multiplications (1976), as cited in Lower Bound of 22 for 3x3 Matrix Multiplication over the Integers, arXiv:2610.01639, Sec. 1 and Sec. 7 (upper bound 23); the integer coefficients 0, 1, -1 make it valid over every commutative ring

explanation.summary: The theorem shows that the tensor rank of 3×3 matrix multiplication over any commutative ring R is at most 23 by exhibiting Laderman's 1976 decomposition consisting of 23 explicit triads with coefficients in {-1, 0, 1}. Validity is verified entry-by-entry: after reducing to the 9 matrix positions, each entry simplifies to an algebraic identity in the coefficients of the input matrices, verified by ring normalization. Packaging this list along with its length equality proves the tensor rank bound.

steps.claim: An explicit list of 23 triads of 3×3 matrices is defined over any commutative ring R.
steps.explanation: We construct Laderman's 23 triples of 3×3 matrices (u, v, w) with coefficients in {0, 1, -1}.

steps.claim: The triad list matrix3_triads_23 has length 23.
steps.explanation: The length of the list is 23 by definition (refl).
steps.code: theorem matrix3_triads_23_length (R : Type*) [CommRing R] : (matrix3_triads_23 R).length = 23 := rfl

steps.claim: It suffices to show that for any two 3×3 matrices A and B and any indices i, j ∈ Fin 3, the (i, j)-th entry of the decomposition's evaluation matches (A * B) i j.
steps.explanation: We introduce arbitrary matrices A and B, then use matrix extensionality to reduce the equality of the two 3×3 matrices to showing their entries agree at every row i and column j.
steps.code:
theorem matrix3_triads_23_valid (R : Type*) [CommRing R] :
    is_valid_matrix3_decomposition (matrix3_triads_23 R) := by
  set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
  intro A B
  ext i j

steps.claim: The (i, j)-th entry of the decomposition is expanded as the sum of the triad products.
steps.explanation: We rewrite the left-hand side using eval_matrix3_decomposition_apply, expressing the entry as the sum over all 23 triads of the scalar product of A with u, times the scalar product of B with v, scaled by the (i, j)-th entry of w.
steps.code: rw [eval_matrix3_decomposition_apply]

  · rintro h ⟨L, hlen, hL⟩

    omega

declarations.name: matrix3_tensor_rank_le_of_surjective
declarations.informal: If f : R → S is a surjective homomorphism of commutative semirings and 3x3 matrix multiplication over R has a valid triad decomposition with at most r products, then so does 3x3 matrix multiplication over S (apply f to every coefficient).
declarations.statement: theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_le_of_surjective {R S : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S] (f : R →+* S) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (r : ℕ) (h : matrix3_tensor_rank_le R r) : matrix3_tensor_rank_le S r
declarations.source:
/-- The image of a triad under a ring homomorphism, entrywise. -/
def matrix3_triad_map {R S : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S] (f : R →+* S)
    (t : Matrix3Triad R) : Matrix3Triad S :=
  ⟨t.u.map f, t.v.map f, t.w.map f⟩

/-- Evaluating a decomposition commutes with applying a ring homomorphism. -/
theorem eval_matrix3_decomposition_map {R S : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S]
    (f : R →+* S) (L : List (Matrix3Triad R)) (A B : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) R) :
    (eval_matrix3_decomposition L A B).map f =
      eval_matrix3_decomposition (L.map (matrix3_triad_map f)) (A.map f) (B.map f) := by
  ext i j
  rw [Matrix.map_apply, eval_matrix3_decomposition_apply, eval_matrix3_decomposition_apply,
    map_list_sum, List.map_map, List.map_map]
  congr 1
  apply List.map_congr_left
  intro t _
  simp [matrix3_triad_map, map_sum, map_mul]

/-- A valid decomposition stays valid under a surjective ring homomorphism. -/
theorem is_valid_matrix3_decomposition_map {R S : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S]
    (f : R →+* S) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (L : List (Matrix3Triad R))
    (hL : is_valid_matrix3_decomposition L) :
    is_valid_matrix3_decomposition (L.map (matrix3_triad_map f)) := by
  intro A' B'
  obtain ⟨A, rfl⟩ : ∃ A : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) R, A.map f = A' :=
    ⟨fun i j => (hf (A' i j)).choose, by ext i j; exact (hf (A' i j)).choose_spec⟩
  obtain ⟨B, rfl⟩ : ∃ B : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) R, B.map f = B' :=
    ⟨fun i j => (hf (B' i j)).choose, by ext i j; exact (hf (B' i j)).choose_spec⟩
  rw [← eval_matrix3_decomposition_map, hL A B, Matrix.map_mul]

theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_le_of_surjective {R S : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S] (f : R →+* S) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (r : ℕ) (h : matrix3_tensor_rank_le R r) : matrix3_tensor_rank_le S r := by
  obtain ⟨L, hlen, hL⟩ := h
  exact ⟨L.map (matrix3_triad_map f), by simpa using hlen, is_valid_matrix3_decomposition_map f hf L hL⟩

explanation.summary: To show that the 3x3 matrix multiplication tensor rank over S is at most r, we map a minimal triad decomposition over R entrywise under the surjective homomorphism f. First, evaluating a decomposition commutes with applying f because ring homomorphisms preserve all operations in the evaluation formula. Second, the mapped decomposition remains valid over S because surjectivity guarantees that any pair of matrices over S lifts to preimages over R, where the decomposition is known to compute their product. Finally, mapping preserves the length of the list of triads, so the resulting decomposition over S has length at most r.

def matrix3_triad_map {R S : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S] (f : R →+* S)

  ⟨t.u.map f, t.v.map f, t.w.map f⟩

steps.explanation: To show that decomposition evaluation commutes with f, we use matrix extensionality (ext i j) and rewrite both sides entrywise using Matrix.map_apply and eval_matrix3_decomposition_apply. Because f is a homomorphism, it commutes with the list sum (map_list_sum) and list mapping composition (List.map_map), leaving an equality of sums over L.

    (eval_matrix3_decomposition L A B).map f =
      eval_matrix3_decomposition (L.map (matrix3_triad_map f)) (A.map f) (B.map f) := by
  ext i j
  rw [Matrix.map_apply, eval_matrix3_decomposition_apply, eval_matrix3_decomposition_apply,
    map_list_sum, List.map_map, List.map_map]

steps.explanation: Using congruence on the list summation (congr 1 and List.map_congr_left), it suffices to check that each triad's contribution commutes with f. Since f preserves addition and multiplication (map_sum and map_mul), simplifying with the definition of matrix3_triad_map shows that the scalar products and scaling commute with f.

  intro t _

steps.claim: Every pair of matrices over S can be lifted entrywise to preimages over R.
steps.explanation: To show that the mapped decomposition is valid over S, let A', B' be arbitrary 3x3 matrices over S. By the surjectivity of f (hf), every entry has a preimage in R, giving preimages A, B over R such that A.map f = A' and B.map f = B'.

    (hL : is_valid_matrix3_decomposition L) :

  obtain ⟨A, rfl⟩ : ∃ A : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) R, A.map f = A' :=

Since this reduction modulo 2 is surjective by ZMod.intCast_surjective, the given integer decomposition of length at most r (h) projects entrywise to a valid decomposition of the same length over ℤ/2ℤ.

glossary.matrix3_tensor_rank_le_of_surjective: A surjective ring homomorphism between commutative semirings transfers bounds on 3x3 matrix multiplication rank: if the tensor rank over the source ring is at most r, it is at most r over the target ring.
glossary.Int.castRingHom: The canonical ring homomorphism from the integers ℤ into any target ring R, mapping an integer to its image in R.
glossary.ZMod.intCast_surjective: The canonical projection from ℤ to ℤ/nℤ is surjective.

declarations.name: matrix3_tensor_rank_int_ge_of_zmod2
declarations.informal: A lower bound r on the number of products of every bilinear algorithm for 3x3 matrix multiplication over the two-element field is also a lower bound over the integers.
declarations.statement: theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_int_ge_of_zmod2 (r : ℕ) (h : matrix3_tensor_rank_ge (ZMod 2) r) : matrix3_tensor_rank_ge ℤ r

declarations.citation: Lower Bound of 22 for 3x3 Matrix Multiplication over the Integers, arXiv:2610.01639, Sec. 5.3 (lower bounds over the two-element field bound algorithms with integer constants)

explanation.summary: The result follows by transferring the lower bound across the canonical quotient homomorphism from the integers to the two-element field ℤ → ℤ/2ℤ. By matrix3_tensor_rank_ge_of_surjective, tensor rank lower bounds are preserved under surjective ring homomorphisms. Because the reduction modulo 2 is surjective (ZMod.intCast_surjective), the lower bound r over ℤ/2ℤ immediately implies the same lower bound over ℤ.

steps.claim: Every bilinear algorithm for 3×3 matrix multiplication over the integers ℤ requires at least r products.
steps.explanation: We apply the general transfer theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_ge_of_surjective to the canonical ring homomorphism from ℤ to ℤ/2ℤ (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2)). Because every residue class modulo 2 contains an integer, this map is surjective by ZMod.intCast_surjective. If there were a decomposition of 3×3 matrix multiplication over ℤ using fewer than r products, projecting its coefficients modulo 2 would yield a valid decomposition over ℤ/2ℤ of the same length, contradicting the hypothesis h.
steps.code: theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_int_ge_of_zmod2 (r : ℕ) (h : matrix3_tensor_rank_ge (ZMod 2) r) : matrix3_tensor_rank_ge ℤ r := matrix3_tensor_rank_ge_of_surjective (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2)) ZMod.intCast_surjective r h

glossary.matrix3_tensor_rank_ge_of_surjective: If f : R →+* S is a surjective ring homomorphism and every bilinear decomposition for 3×3 matrix multiplication over S requires at least r products, then every such decomposition over R also requires at least r products.
glossary.ZMod.intCast_surjective: The canonical ring homomorphism from the integers to ℤ/nℤ is surjective.

declarations.name: gf8_oracle_syndrome
declarations.informal: The syndrome s_A of the GF(8) multiplication phase oracle U_3 |x, y, z> = (-1)^{z . (x * y)} |x, y, z> on nine qubits: s_A = 1 iff A = {x_q, y_r, z_l} (qubit q, qubit 3 + r, qubit 6 + l) and bit l of alpha^q * alpha^r in GF(8) = F_2[alpha]/(alpha^3 + alpha + 1) is 1; s_A = 0 for every other subset A (the oracle is pure-cubic). By the moment form of the Amy-Mosca correspondence, the T-count of U_3 is the least size of a set of nonzero parities whose order-1, 2, 3 moments equal this syndrome.
declarations.statement: def gf8_oracle_syndrome (A : Finset (Fin 9)) : ZMod 2
declarations.source:
/-- The order-at-most-three syndrome of the GF(8) multiplication phase oracle on nine qubits (qubits 0-2 hold x, 3-5 hold y, 6-8 hold z, polynomial basis with alpha^3 = alpha + 1): 1 exactly on the triples {x_q, y_r, z_l} for which bit l of alpha^q * alpha^r is 1, and 0 on every other set. -/
def gf8_oracle_syndrome (A : Finset (Fin 9)) : ZMod 2 :=
  if ∃ q r l : Fin 3, gf8_mult_coeff q r l = 1 ∧
      A = {⟨q.val, by omega⟩, ⟨3 + r.val, by omega⟩, ⟨6 + l.val, by omega⟩} then 1 else 0
declarations.citation: Exact T-counts of Toffoli Layers from an Isotropy Bound, arXiv:2610.01024, Proposition 55 and Fact 21 (the GF(8) multiplication phase oracle and its syndrome)

Unfolding the definition reduces this to an existential search over indices $q, r, l \in \{0, 1, 2\}$, which is satisfied by the choice $q = r = l = 0$. Since all types and predicates involved are finite and decidable, the proof is closed by direct computation.

steps.claim: The oracle syndrome on the subset $\{0, 3, 6\}$ evaluates to $1$.
steps.explanation: By definition, $\text{gf8\_oracle\_syndrome}(\{0, 3, 6\}) = 1$ if there exist indices $q, r, l \in \text{Fin } 3$ such that $\{q, 3 + r, 6 + l\} = \{0, 3, 6\}$ and $\text{gf8\_mult\_coeff}(q, r, l) = 1$. The witness $q = 0, r = 0, l = 0$ satisfies both conditions, since $\{0, 3, 6\} = \{0, 3, 6\}$ and $\text{gf8\_mult\_coeff}(0, 0, 0) = 1$ (the $(0+0, 0) = (0, 0)$ branch of the definition). Because this search is over finite types, the `decide` tactic completes the proof by direct evaluation.
