declarations.name: schwartz_zippel_nonzero_count_ge
declarations.informal: Let F be an integral domain, S a nonempty finite subset of F, n a positive integer, and p a nonzero polynomial in n variables over F of total degree d. Then the number of points of S^n at which p does not vanish is at least |S|^n − d·|S|^(n−1); equivalently, at least a fraction 1 − d/|S| of the points of S^n are nonzero for p. This is the guarantee of the random-evaluation identity test: a point where p is nonzero certifies p ≠ 0, so the test has one-sided error and rejects a nonzero p with probability at most d/|S|.
declarations.source:
open scoped Finset in
/-- At least |S|^n − d·|S|^(n−1) points of S^n are nonzero for a nonzero polynomial of total degree d. -/
theorem schwartz_zippel_nonzero_count_ge {F : Type*} [CommRing F] [IsDomain F] [DecidableEq F]
    {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F} (hp : p ≠ 0) {S : Finset F}
    (hS : 0 < S.card) :
    S.card ^ n - p.totalDegree * S.card ^ (n - 1)
      ≤ #{x ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S) | MvPolynomial.eval x p ≠ 0} := by
  have h_le := schwartz_zippel_zero_count_le hn hp hS
  have h_sum := Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not (s := Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S))
    (fun x => MvPolynomial.eval x p = 0)
  simp only [Fintype.card_piFinset, Finset.prod_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin] at h_sum
  simp only [ne_eq]
  omega
declarations.citation: Schwartz 1980; Zippel 1979, in the one-sided-error form used for the randomized identity test (Motwani & Raghavan, Randomized Algorithms, ch. 7); companion of the knowledge-base node `schwartz_zippel_exists_nonzero_eval`.
declarations.reading: The declaration universally quantifies over a type `F` carrying a commutative ring structure, an integral-domain structure, and decidable equality; over a natural number `n` with `0 < n`; over a nonzero multivariate polynomial `p` in `n` variables over `F`; and over a finite subset `S` of `F` with `0 < S.card`. It asserts that the number of `n`-tuples `x : Fin n → F` whose coordinates all lie in `S` and at which `p` evaluates to a nonzero element is at least `S.card ^ n - p.totalDegree * S.card ^ (n - 1)`, where `p.totalDegree` is the total degree of `p` and the subtraction is the truncated subtraction of natural numbers. Equivalently, the count is at least `max(0, |S|^n - deg(p) * |S|^(n-1))`.

declarations.name: schwartz_zippel_repeated_trials_zero_count_le
declarations.informal: Let F be an integral domain, S a nonempty finite subset of F, n a positive integer, and p a nonzero polynomial in n variables over F of total degree d. Then for every t the number of t-tuples (x_1, …, x_t) of points of S^n at which p vanishes at every one of the t coordinates is at most (d·|S|^(n−1))^t; equivalently, t independent random trials of the evaluation test all fail with probability at most (d/|S|)^t.
declarations.statement:
open scoped Finset in
theorem schwartz_zippel_repeated_trials_zero_count_le {F : Type*} [CommRing F] [IsDomain F]
    [DecidableEq F] {n t : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F} (hp : p ≠ 0)
    {S : Finset F} (hS : 0 < S.card) :
    #{X ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin t => Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S)) |
        ∀ i, MvPolynomial.eval (X i) p = 0}
      ≤ (p.totalDegree * S.card ^ (n - 1)) ^ t
declarations.source:
open scoped Finset in
/-- Amplification by repetition: the number of t-tuples of points of S^n that are all zeros of a nonzero polynomial of total degree d is at most (d·|S|^(n−1))^t. -/
theorem schwartz_zippel_repeated_trials_zero_count_le {F : Type*} [CommRing F] [IsDomain F]
    [DecidableEq F] {n t : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F} (hp : p ≠ 0)
    {S : Finset F} (hS : 0 < S.card) :
    #{X ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin t => Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S)) |
        ∀ i, MvPolynomial.eval (X i) p = 0}
      ≤ (p.totalDegree * S.card ^ (n - 1)) ^ t := by
  have h_set :
    {X ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin t => Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S)) |
        ∀ i, MvPolynomial.eval (X i) p = 0} =
    Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin t =>
      {x ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S) | MvPolynomial.eval x p = 0}) := by
    ext X
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Fintype.mem_piFinset]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩ i
      exact ⟨h1 i, h2 i⟩
    · intro h
      exact ⟨fun i => (h i).1, fun i => (h i).2⟩
  rw [h_set, Fintype.card_piFinset_const]
  exact Nat.pow_le_pow_left (schwartz_zippel_zero_count_le hn hp hS) t
declarations.citation: Amplification by independent repetition of the random-evaluation identity test of Schwartz 1980 / Zippel 1979 (Motwani & Raghavan, Randomized Algorithms, ch. 7). Concepts anchored by Mathlib `MvPolynomial.schwartz_zippel_totalDegree`.
declarations.reading:
For every type `F` with a commutative ring structure, an integral domain structure, and decidable equality, for all natural numbers `n` and `t` with `n > 0`, for every nonzero polynomial `p` in `n` variables over `F`, and every finite subset `S` of `F` with positive cardinality, the number of `t`-tuples of points of `S^n` at which `p` vanishes is at most `(p.totalDegree * |S|^(n-1))^t`.

More explicitly, the tuples are functions `X : Fin t → (Fin n → F)` such that every coordinate `X j i` lies in `S`, and the vanishing condition is that for every `j : Fin t`, the evaluation of `p` at the assignment `X j : Fin n → F` is zero. The bound parses as `(p.totalDegree * (S.card ^ (n - 1))) ^ t`, because `^` binds more tightly than `*`; the outer exponent `t` applies to the whole product.

declarations.name: regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching
declarations.informal: Every d-regular bipartite simple graph on a finite vertex set, with degree d > 0, has a perfect matching.
declarations.statement:
theorem regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d)
    (hreg : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) (hbip : G.IsBipartite) :
    ∃ M : SimpleGraph.Subgraph G, M.IsPerfectMatching
declarations.source:
open scoped Classical
open SimpleGraph Finset Set

lemma regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching_card_le_card_biUnion {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d)
    (hreg : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) (S : Finset V) :
    #S ≤ #(S.biUnion (fun x => G.neighborFinset x)) := by
  let T := S.biUnion (fun x => G.neighborFinset x)
  have h_deg (v : V) : #(G.neighborFinset v) = d := by
    rw [card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
    exact hreg v
  have h_above (u : V) (hu : u ∈ S) : #(bipartiteAbove G.Adj T u) = d := by
    have : bipartiteAbove G.Adj T u = G.neighborFinset u := by
      ext v
      simp only [bipartiteAbove, mem_filter, mem_neighborFinset]
      constructor
      · intro ⟨_, hadj⟩
        exact hadj
      · intro hadj
        refine ⟨?_, hadj⟩
        rw [Finset.mem_biUnion]
        exact ⟨u, hu, G.mem_neighborFinset u v |>.mpr hadj⟩
    rw [this, h_deg]
  have h_below (v : V) : #(bipartiteBelow G.Adj S v) ≤ d := by
    have : bipartiteBelow G.Adj S v ⊆ G.neighborFinset v := by
      intro u hu
      simp only [bipartiteBelow, mem_filter] at hu
      simp only [mem_neighborFinset]
      exact hu.2.symm
    exact (Finset.card_le_card this).trans (h_deg v).le
  have h_sum_above : ∑ u ∈ S, #(bipartiteAbove G.Adj T u) = #S * d := by
    rw [sum_congr rfl h_above]
    simp
  have h_sum_below : ∑ v ∈ T, #(bipartiteBelow G.Adj S v) ≤ #T * d := by
    calc ∑ v ∈ T, #(bipartiteBelow G.Adj S v)
      _ ≤ ∑ v ∈ T, d := sum_le_sum fun v _ => h_below v
      _ = #T * d := by simp
  have h_eq := sum_card_bipartiteAbove_eq_sum_card_bipartiteBelow G.Adj (s := S) (t := T)
  have h_mul_le : #S * d ≤ #T * d := by
    rw [← h_sum_above, h_eq]
    exact h_sum_below
  exact Nat.le_of_mul_le_mul_right h_mul_le hd

lemma regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching_ncard_le_ncard_biUnion {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d)
    (hreg : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) (s : Set V) :
    s.ncard ≤ (⋃ x ∈ s, G.neighborSet x).ncard := by
  have h_eq : (⋃ x ∈ s, G.neighborSet x).toFinset = s.toFinset.biUnion (fun x => G.neighborFinset x) := by
    ext v
    simp
  rw [Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card' s, Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card' _, h_eq]
  exact regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching_card_le_card_biUnion G hd hreg s.toFinset

/-- Every d-regular bipartite graph with d > 0 has a perfect matching. -/
theorem regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d)
    (hreg : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) (hbip : G.IsBipartite) :
    ∃ M : SimpleGraph.Subgraph G, M.IsPerfectMatching := by
  obtain ⟨p₁, p₂, hbipW⟩ := hbip.exists_isBipartiteWith
  exact exists_isPerfectMatching_of_forall_ncard_le hbipW
    (fun s => regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching_ncard_le_ncard_biUnion G hd hreg s)
declarations.citation: Diestel, Graph Theory, Corollary 2.1.3
declarations.reading: For any finite type `V`, any simple graph `G` on `V`, and any natural number `d` such that `0 < d`, if `G` is regular of degree `d` (every vertex in `V` has degree `d`) and `G` is bipartite (2-colorable), then there exists a subgraph `M` of `G` that is a perfect matching of `G` (that is, `M` spans all vertices of `V` and every vertex has degree 1 in `M`).

declarations.name: is_tree_iff_is_acyclic_and_card
declarations.informal: A simple graph G on a finite vertex type V is a tree if and only if G is acyclic and the number of edges plus 1 equals the number of vertices.
declarations.statement:
theorem is_tree_iff_is_acyclic_and_card {V : Type*} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    G.IsTree ↔ G.IsAcyclic ∧ Nat.card G.edgeSet + 1 = Nat.card V
declarations.source:
/-- A finite graph is a tree if and only if it is acyclic and |E| + 1 = |V|. -/
theorem is_tree_iff_is_acyclic_and_card {V : Type*} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    G.IsTree ↔ G.IsAcyclic ∧ Nat.card G.edgeSet + 1 = Nat.card V := by
  refine ⟨fun h ↦ ⟨h.isAcyclic, (SimpleGraph.isTree_iff_connected_and_card.mp h).2⟩, fun h ↦ ?_⟩
  cases isEmpty_or_nonempty V
  · exfalso
    have : Nat.card V = 0 := Nat.card_eq_zero.mpr (Or.inl ‹IsEmpty V›)
    omega
  · obtain ⟨F, hGF, -, hFTree⟩ :=
      SimpleGraph.connected_top.exists_isTree_le_of_le_of_isAcyclic (le_top : G ≤ ⊤) h.1
    have hFcard : Nat.card F.edgeSet + 1 = Nat.card V :=
      (SimpleGraph.isTree_iff_connected_and_card.mp hFTree).2
    have hcard : Nat.card F.edgeSet ≤ Nat.card G.edgeSet := by omega
    have hsub : G.edgeSet ⊆ F.edgeSet := SimpleGraph.edgeSet_mono hGF
    have heq : G.edgeSet = F.edgeSet :=
      Set.Finite.eq_of_subset_of_card_le (Set.toFinite F.edgeSet) hsub hcard
    have : G = F := SimpleGraph.edgeSet_injective heq
    rw [this]
    exact hFTree
declarations.citation: Diestel, Graph Theory, Theorem 1.5.1
declarations.reading: For any finite type `V` and any simple graph `G` on `V`, `G` is a tree (`G.IsTree`) if and only if `G` is acyclic (`G.IsAcyclic`) and the number of edges in `G` plus one equals the number of vertices in `V` (`Nat.card G.edgeSet + 1 = Nat.card V`).

declarations.name: canonical_partition_function_pos
declarations.informal: For any nonempty finite configuration space Ω, Hamiltonian H : Ω → ℝ, and inverse temperature β, the canonical partition function is strictly positive.

theorem canonical_partition_function_pos {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Nonempty Ω] (H : Ω → ℝ) (β : ℝ) :
    0 < canonicalPartitionFunction H β
declarations.source:
/-- The canonical partition function of a nonempty finite system is strictly positive. -/
theorem canonical_partition_function_pos {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Nonempty Ω] (H : Ω → ℝ) (β : ℝ) :
    0 < canonicalPartitionFunction H β := by
  unfold canonicalPartitionFunction
  obtain ⟨ω₀⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty Ω)
  exact Finset.sum_pos' (fun ω _ => (Real.exp_pos _).le) ⟨ω₀, Finset.mem_univ ω₀, Real.exp_pos _⟩

declarations.name: boltzmann_distribution_sum_eq_one
declarations.informal: For any nonempty finite configuration space Ω, Hamiltonian H : Ω → ℝ, and inverse temperature β, the sum of the Boltzmann distribution over all configurations is equal to 1.
declarations.statement:
theorem boltzmann_distribution_sum_eq_one {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Nonempty Ω] (H : Ω → ℝ) (β : ℝ) :
    ∑ ω : Ω, boltzmannDistribution H β ω = 1
declarations.source:
/-- The Boltzmann distribution sums to 1 over the configuration space. -/
theorem boltzmann_distribution_sum_eq_one {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Nonempty Ω] (H : Ω → ℝ) (β : ℝ) :
    ∑ ω : Ω, boltzmannDistribution H β ω = 1 := by
  have hpos := canonical_partition_function_pos H β
  dsimp [boltzmannDistribution]
  rw [← Finset.sum_div]
  exact div_self hpos.ne'

declarations.name: resolution_refutation_exists_of_unsat
declarations.informal: Completeness of resolution, the length-free part of the problem: every unsatisfiable CNF formula has a resolution refutation.
declarations.statement: theorem resolution_refutation_exists_of_unsat (F : Finset (Finset (CnfLit ℕ))) (h : ¬ CnfSatisfiable (F.toList.map Finset.toList)) : ∃ π, is_resolution_refutation F π
declarations.source:
/-- The variable of a literal. -/
def resolution_lit_var {V : Type*} : CnfLit V → V
  | CnfLit.pos v => v
  | CnfLit.neg v => v


/-- One step of a resolution derivation, for a sequence indexed by `ℕ`. -/
def resolution_step_at {V : Type*} (F : Finset (Finset (CnfLit V)))
    (f : ℕ → Finset (CnfLit V)) (i : ℕ) : Prop :=
  f i ∈ F ∨ (∃ j < i, f j ⊆ f i) ∨
  (∃ j < i, ∃ k < i, ∃ (x : V) (C D : Finset (CnfLit V)),
    (∀ l, l ∈ f j ↔ l ∈ C ∨ l = CnfLit.pos x) ∧ (∀ l, l ∈ f k ↔ l ∈ D ∨ l = CnfLit.neg x) ∧
    (∀ l, l ∈ f i ↔ l ∈ C ∨ l ∈ D))

theorem resolution_step_at_transport {V : Type*} {F : Finset (Finset (CnfLit V))}
    {f g : ℕ → Finset (CnfLit V)} {i : ℕ} (σ : ℕ → ℕ) (hσ : ∀ j < i, σ j < σ i)
    (hg : ∀ j ≤ i, g (σ j) = f j) (h : resolution_step_at F f i) :
    resolution_step_at F g (σ i) := by
  rcases h with h | ⟨j, hj, h⟩ | ⟨j, hj, k, hk, x, C, D, h1, h2, h3⟩
  · left; rw [hg i le_rfl]; exact h
  · right; left; exact ⟨σ j, hσ j hj, by rw [hg j hj.le, hg i le_rfl]; exact h⟩
  · right; right
    refine ⟨σ j, hσ j hj, σ k, hσ k hk, x, C, D, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [hg j hj.le]; exact h1
    · rw [hg k hk.le]; exact h2
    · rw [hg i le_rfl]; exact h3

/-- The sequence of a list, padded with the empty clause. -/
def resolution_seq {V : Type*} (π : List (Finset (CnfLit V))) (k : ℕ) : Finset (CnfLit V) :=
  (π[k]?).getD ∅

theorem resolution_seq_of_lt {V : Type*} (π : List (Finset (CnfLit V))) {k : ℕ}
    (hk : k < π.length) : resolution_seq π k = π[k] := by
  simp [resolution_seq, List.getElem?_eq_getElem hk]

theorem is_resolution_derivation_of_steps {V : Type*} (F : Finset (Finset (CnfLit V)))
    (π : List (Finset (CnfLit V)))
    (h : ∀ i < π.length, resolution_step_at F (resolution_seq π) i) :
    is_resolution_derivation F π := by
  intro i
  have hi := i.isLt
  rcases h i.val hi with h | ⟨j, hj, h⟩ | ⟨j, hj, k, hk, x, C, D, h1, h2, h3⟩
  · left; rw [resolution_seq_of_lt π hi] at h; simpa using h
  · right; left
    refine ⟨⟨j, by omega⟩, by simp [Fin.lt_def, hj], ?_⟩
    rw [resolution_seq_of_lt π hi, resolution_seq_of_lt π (by omega)] at h
    simpa using h
  · right; right
    refine ⟨⟨j, by omega⟩, ⟨k, by omega⟩, by simp [Fin.lt_def, hj], by simp [Fin.lt_def, hk],
      x, C, D, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [resolution_seq_of_lt π (by omega)] at h1; simpa using h1
    · rw [resolution_seq_of_lt π (by omega)] at h2; simpa using h2
    · rw [resolution_seq_of_lt π hi] at h3; simpa using h3

/-- Tree-like resolution derivability. -/
inductive ResolutionDerivable {V : Type*} (F : Finset (Finset (CnfLit V))) :
    Finset (CnfLit V) → Prop
  | ax {C : Finset (CnfLit V)} : C ∈ F → ResolutionDerivable F C
  | weak {C E : Finset (CnfLit V)} : ResolutionDerivable F C → C ⊆ E → ResolutionDerivable F E
  | res {x : V} {A B C D E : Finset (CnfLit V)} : ResolutionDerivable F A →
      ResolutionDerivable F B → (∀ l, l ∈ A ↔ l ∈ C ∨ l = CnfLit.pos x) →
      (∀ l, l ∈ B ↔ l ∈ D ∨ l = CnfLit.neg x) → (∀ l, l ∈ E ↔ l ∈ C ∨ l ∈ D) →
      ResolutionDerivable F E

theorem resolution_seq_append_left {V : Type*} (π ρ : List (Finset (CnfLit V))) {k : ℕ}
    (hk : k < π.length) : resolution_seq (π ++ ρ) k = resolution_seq π k := by
  simp [resolution_seq, List.getElem?_append_left hk]

theorem resolution_seq_append_right {V : Type*} (π ρ : List (Finset (CnfLit V))) (k : ℕ) :
    resolution_seq (π ++ ρ) (k + π.length) = resolution_seq ρ k := by
  simp [resolution_seq, List.getElem?_append_right (Nat.le_add_left _ _)]

/-- Steps of `π` stay steps of `π ++ ρ`. -/
theorem resolution_steps_append_left {V : Type*} (F : Finset (Finset (CnfLit V)))
    (π ρ : List (Finset (CnfLit V)))
    (h : ∀ i < π.length, resolution_step_at F (resolution_seq π) i) :
    ∀ i < π.length, resolution_step_at F (resolution_seq (π ++ ρ)) i := by
  intro i hi
  exact resolution_step_at_transport id (fun j hj => hj)
    (fun j hj => by simp only [id]; exact resolution_seq_append_left π ρ (by omega)) (h i hi)

/-- Steps of `ρ` become steps of `π ++ ρ`, shifted by `π.length`. -/
theorem resolution_steps_append_right {V : Type*} (F : Finset (Finset (CnfLit V)))
    (π ρ : List (Finset (CnfLit V)))
    (h : ∀ i < ρ.length, resolution_step_at F (resolution_seq ρ) i) :
    ∀ i < ρ.length, resolution_step_at F (resolution_seq (π ++ ρ)) (i + π.length) := by
  intro i hi
  exact resolution_step_at_transport (· + π.length) (fun j hj => by show j + π.length < i + π.length; omega)
    (fun j _ => resolution_seq_append_right π ρ j) (h i hi)

theorem resolution_derivable_seq {V : Type*} {F : Finset (Finset (CnfLit V))}
    {E : Finset (CnfLit V)} (h : ResolutionDerivable F E) :
    ∃ π : List (Finset (CnfLit V)), ∃ n, π.length = n + 1 ∧ resolution_seq π n = E ∧
      ∀ i < π.length, resolution_step_at F (resolution_seq π) i := by
  induction h with
  | @ax C hC =>
    refine ⟨[C], 0, rfl, by simp [resolution_seq], ?_⟩
    intro i hi
    have : i = 0 := by simpa using hi
    subst this
    left; simpa [resolution_seq] using hC
  | @weak C E _ hCE ih =>
    obtain ⟨π, n, hlen, hlast, hsteps⟩ := ih
    refine ⟨π ++ [E], n + 1, by simp [hlen], ?_, ?_⟩
    · have := resolution_seq_append_right π [E] 0
      rw [show n + 1 = 0 + π.length by omega, this]; simp [resolution_seq]
    · intro i hi
      simp only [List.length_append, List.length_singleton] at hi
      by_cases hin : i < π.length
      · exact resolution_steps_append_left F π [E] hsteps i hin
      · have hi' : i = n + 1 := by omega
        subst hi'
        right; left
        refine ⟨n, by omega, ?_⟩
        rw [resolution_seq_append_left π [E] (by omega), hlast]
        have := resolution_seq_append_right π [E] 0
        rw [show 0 + π.length = n + 1 by omega] at this
        rw [this]; simpa [resolution_seq] using hCE
  | @res x A B C D E _ _ hA hB hE ihA ihB =>
    obtain ⟨π, n, hlen, hlast, hsteps⟩ := ihA
    obtain ⟨ρ, m, hlen', hlast', hsteps'⟩ := ihB
    refine ⟨π ++ ρ ++ [E], n + m + 2, by simp [hlen, hlen']; omega, ?_, ?_⟩
    · have := resolution_seq_append_right (π ++ ρ) [E] 0
      rw [show n + m + 2 = 0 + (π ++ ρ).length by simp; omega, this]; simp [resolution_seq]
    · intro i hi
      simp only [List.length_append, List.length_singleton] at hi
      by_cases h1 : i < π.length
      · have := resolution_steps_append_left F π ρ hsteps i h1
        exact resolution_steps_append_left F (π ++ ρ) [E] (fun i hi => by
          by_cases h1' : i < π.length
          · exact resolution_steps_append_left F π ρ hsteps i h1'
          · have := resolution_steps_append_right F π ρ hsteps' (i - π.length)
              (by simp at hi; omega)
            rwa [Nat.sub_add_cancel (by omega)] at this) i (by simp; omega)
      · by_cases h2 : i < π.length + ρ.length
        · have := resolution_steps_append_right F π ρ hsteps' (i - π.length) (by omega)
          rw [Nat.sub_add_cancel (by omega)] at this
          exact resolution_steps_append_left F (π ++ ρ) [E] (fun i hi => by
            by_cases h1' : i < π.length
            · exact resolution_steps_append_left F π ρ hsteps i h1'
            · have := resolution_steps_append_right F π ρ hsteps' (i - π.length)
                (by simp at hi; omega)
              rwa [Nat.sub_add_cancel (by omega)] at this) i (by simp; omega)
        · have hi' : i = n + m + 2 := by omega
          subst hi'
          right; right
          refine ⟨n, by omega, n + 1 + m, by omega, x, C, D, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
          · rw [resolution_seq_append_left _ _ (by simp; omega),
              resolution_seq_append_left _ _ (by omega), hlast]
            exact hA
          · rw [resolution_seq_append_left _ _ (by simp; omega)]
            have := resolution_seq_append_right π ρ m
            rw [show m + π.length = n + 1 + m by omega] at this
            rw [this, hlast']
            exact hB
          · have := resolution_seq_append_right (π ++ ρ) [E] 0
            rw [show 0 + (π ++ ρ).length = n + m + 2 by simp; omega] at this
            rw [this]; simpa [resolution_seq] using hE

/-- A literal is true under an assignment. -/
def resolution_lit_true {V : Type*} (τ : V → Bool) : CnfLit V → Prop
  | CnfLit.pos v => τ v = true
  | CnfLit.neg v => τ v = false

theorem resolution_derivable_of_unsat {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (F : Finset (Finset (CnfLit V)))
    (hF : ∀ τ : V → Bool, ∃ C ∈ F, ∀ l ∈ C, ¬ resolution_lit_true τ l) :
    ∀ (X : Finset V) (K : Finset (CnfLit V)), (∀ v, ¬ (CnfLit.pos v ∈ K ∧ CnfLit.neg v ∈ K)) →
      (∀ C ∈ F, ∀ l ∈ C, resolution_lit_var l ∈ X ∨ CnfLit.pos (resolution_lit_var l) ∈ K ∨
        CnfLit.neg (resolution_lit_var l) ∈ K) →
      ResolutionDerivable F K := by
  classical
  intro X
  induction X using Finset.induction_on with
  | empty =>
    intro K hK hvars
    obtain ⟨C, hCF, hC⟩ := hF (fun v => if CnfLit.pos v ∈ K then false else true)
    refine ResolutionDerivable.weak (ResolutionDerivable.ax hCF) ?_
    intro l hl
    have hfalse := hC l hl
    rcases hvars C hCF l hl with h | h | h
    · simp at h
    · cases l with
      | pos v =>
        simp only [resolution_lit_var] at h; exact h
      | neg v =>
        simp only [resolution_lit_var] at h
        exact (hfalse (by simp [resolution_lit_true, h])).elim
    · cases l with
      | pos v =>
        simp only [resolution_lit_var] at h
        by_contra hpos
        exact hfalse (by simp [resolution_lit_true, hpos])
      | neg v =>
        simp only [resolution_lit_var] at h; exact h
  | @insert x X hx ih =>
    intro K hK hvars
    by_cases hxK : CnfLit.pos x ∈ K ∨ CnfLit.neg x ∈ K
    · apply ih K hK
      intro C hC l hl
      rcases hvars C hC l hl with h | h | h
      · rcases Finset.mem_insert.1 h with h | h
        · rw [h]; exact Or.inr hxK
        · exact Or.inl h
      · exact Or.inr (Or.inl h)
      · exact Or.inr (Or.inr h)
    · push_neg at hxK
      have hsub : ∀ K' : Finset (CnfLit V), K ⊆ K' → (CnfLit.pos x ∈ K' ∨ CnfLit.neg x ∈ K') →
          ∀ C ∈ F, ∀ l ∈ C, resolution_lit_var l ∈ X ∨ CnfLit.pos (resolution_lit_var l) ∈ K' ∨
            CnfLit.neg (resolution_lit_var l) ∈ K' := by
        intro K' hKK' hx' C hC l hl
        rcases hvars C hC l hl with h | h | h
        · rcases Finset.mem_insert.1 h with h | h
          · rw [h]; exact Or.inr hx'
          · exact Or.inl h
        · exact Or.inr (Or.inl (hKK' h))
        · exact Or.inr (Or.inr (hKK' h))
      have h1 := ih (insert (CnfLit.pos x) K) (by
          intro v ⟨hp, hn⟩
          rcases Finset.mem_insert.1 hp with hp | hp <;> rcases Finset.mem_insert.1 hn with hn | hn
          · cases hn
          · cases hp; exact hxK.2 hn
          · cases hn
          · exact hK v ⟨hp, hn⟩)
        (hsub _ (Finset.subset_insert _ _) (Or.inl (Finset.mem_insert_self _ _)))
      have h2 := ih (insert (CnfLit.neg x) K) (by
          intro v ⟨hp, hn⟩
          rcases Finset.mem_insert.1 hp with hp | hp <;> rcases Finset.mem_insert.1 hn with hn | hn
          · cases hp
          · cases hp
          · cases hn; exact hxK.1 hp
          · exact hK v ⟨hp, hn⟩)
        (hsub _ (Finset.subset_insert _ _) (Or.inr (Finset.mem_insert_self _ _)))
      exact ResolutionDerivable.res (x := x) (C := K) (D := K) h1 h2
        (fun l => by simp [Finset.mem_insert, or_comm]) (fun l => by simp [Finset.mem_insert, or_comm])
        (fun l => by simp)

theorem resolution_refutation_exists_of_unsat (F : Finset (Finset (CnfLit ℕ))) (h : ¬ CnfSatisfiable (F.toList.map Finset.toList)) : ∃ π, is_resolution_refutation F π := by
  classical
  have hF : ∀ τ : ℕ → Bool, ∃ C ∈ F, ∀ l ∈ C, ¬ resolution_lit_true τ l := by
    intro τ
    by_contra hne
    push_neg at hne
    apply h
    refine ⟨τ, ?_⟩
    intro c hc
    simp only [List.mem_map, Finset.mem_toList] at hc
    obtain ⟨C, hC, rfl⟩ := hc
    obtain ⟨l, hl, hlt⟩ := hne C hC
    refine ⟨l, by simpa using hl, ?_⟩
    cases l <;> simpa [resolution_lit_true] using hlt
  have hder := resolution_derivable_of_unsat F hF (F.biUnion fun C => C.image resolution_lit_var) ∅
    (by simp) (fun C hC l hl => Or.inl (Finset.mem_biUnion.2 ⟨C, hC, Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ hl⟩))
  obtain ⟨π, n, hlen, hlast, hsteps⟩ := resolution_derivable_seq hder
  refine ⟨π, is_resolution_derivation_of_steps F π hsteps, ?_⟩
  have hn : n < π.length := by omega
  rw [resolution_seq_of_lt π hn] at hlast
  rw [List.getLast?_eq_getElem?, hlen, Nat.add_sub_cancel, List.getElem?_eq_getElem hn, hlast]
declarations.citation: standard textbook result (proof complexity): refutational completeness of resolution, as recalled in arXiv:2610.02047, Sec. 3.1

declarations.name: ejr_committee_exists
declarations.informal: For every approval profile with at least one voter and every committee size k ≤ m, some committee of size k satisfies EJR (for instance the PAV committee).
declarations.statement:
theorem ejr_committee_exists :
    ∀ (n m : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Finset (Fin m)), 0 < n → ∀ k, k ≤ m →
      ∃ W, is_ejr_committee A k W
declarations.source:
/-- The greedy cohesive argument: for every set `S` of voters there is a set `W` of at most
`|S| k / n` candidates such that every `ℓ`-cohesive group inside `S` has a member approving at
least `ℓ` members of `W`. (Take a cohesive group `G ⊆ S` with the largest `ℓ`, give it `ℓ`
commonly approved candidates and recurse on `S \ G`.) -/
theorem ejr_greedy_cohesive_aux {n m : ℕ} (A : Fin n → Finset (Fin m)) (k : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n)
    (S : Finset (Fin n)) : ∃ W : Finset (Fin m), W.card * n ≤ S.card * k ∧
      ∀ ℓ, 1 ≤ ℓ → ∀ G ⊆ S, is_ejr_cohesive_group A k ℓ G → ∃ i ∈ G, ℓ ≤ (A i ∩ W).card := by
  classical
  induction S using Finset.strongInduction with
  | H S ih =>
  have hle_m : ∀ ℓ G, is_ejr_cohesive_group A k ℓ G → ℓ ≤ m := fun ℓ G h =>
    h.2.trans ((Finset.card_le_univ _).trans (by simp))
  let P : Finset (ℕ × Finset (Fin n)) :=
    ((Finset.Icc 1 m) ×ˢ S.powerset).filter fun p => is_ejr_cohesive_group A k p.1 p.2
  have hmemP : ∀ ℓ G, (ℓ, G) ∈ P ↔ (1 ≤ ℓ ∧ G ⊆ S ∧ is_ejr_cohesive_group A k ℓ G) := by
    intro ℓ G
    simp only [P, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_Icc, Finset.mem_powerset]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨⟨⟨h1, -⟩, h2⟩, h3⟩; exact ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩; exact ⟨⟨⟨h1, hle_m ℓ G h3⟩, h2⟩, h3⟩
  by_cases hP : P.Nonempty
  · obtain ⟨⟨ℓ, G⟩, hpP, hmax⟩ := P.exists_max_image Prod.fst hP
    obtain ⟨hℓ1, hGS, hcoh⟩ := (hmemP ℓ G).1 hpP
    have hGne : G.Nonempty := by
      rw [Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty]
      rintro rfl
      have h := hcoh.1
      simp only [Finset.card_empty, zero_mul] at h
      have : 0 < ℓ * n := Nat.mul_pos hℓ1 hn
      omega
    obtain ⟨W', hW'card, hW'⟩ := ih (S \ G) (Finset.sdiff_ssubset hGS hGne)
    obtain ⟨C, hCsub, hCcard⟩ := Finset.exists_subset_card_eq hcoh.2
    refine ⟨W' ∪ C, ?_, ?_⟩
    · have h1 : (W' ∪ C).card ≤ W'.card + ℓ := (Finset.card_union_le _ _).trans (by rw [hCcard])
      have h2 : (S \ G).card + G.card = S.card := Finset.card_sdiff_add_card_eq_card hGS
      have hc := hcoh.1
      calc (W' ∪ C).card * n ≤ (W'.card + ℓ) * n := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ h1
        _ = W'.card * n + ℓ * n := by ring
        _ ≤ (S \ G).card * k + G.card * k := Nat.add_le_add hW'card hc
        _ = S.card * k := by rw [← Nat.add_mul, h2]
    · intro ℓ' hℓ' H hHS hHcoh
      by_cases hHG : Disjoint H G
      · have hHsub : H ⊆ S \ G := fun x hx =>
          Finset.mem_sdiff.2 ⟨hHS hx, Finset.disjoint_left.1 hHG hx⟩
        obtain ⟨i, hi, hle⟩ := hW' ℓ' hℓ' H hHsub hHcoh
        exact ⟨i, hi, hle.trans (Finset.card_le_card
          (Finset.inter_subset_inter_left Finset.subset_union_left))⟩
      · obtain ⟨i, hiH, hiG⟩ := Finset.not_disjoint_iff.1 hHG
        have hℓ'le : ℓ' ≤ ℓ := hmax (ℓ', H) ((hmemP ℓ' H).2 ⟨hℓ', hHS, hHcoh⟩)
        refine ⟨i, hiH, hℓ'le.trans ?_⟩
        rw [← hCcard]
        apply Finset.card_le_card
        intro c hc
        exact Finset.mem_inter.2 ⟨(Finset.mem_filter.1 (hCsub hc)).2 i hiG,
          Finset.mem_union_right _ hc⟩
  · refine ⟨∅, by simp, ?_⟩
    intro ℓ hℓ G hGS hcoh
    exact absurd ⟨(ℓ, G), (hmemP ℓ G).2 ⟨hℓ, hGS, hcoh⟩⟩ hP

theorem ejr_committee_exists :
    ∀ (n m : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Finset (Fin m)), 0 < n → ∀ k, k ≤ m →
      ∃ W, is_ejr_committee A k W := by
  intro n m A hn k hk
  classical
  obtain ⟨W, hWc, hW⟩ := ejr_greedy_cohesive_aux A k hn Finset.univ
  have hWk : W.card ≤ k := by
    rw [Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin] at hWc
    exact Nat.le_of_mul_le_mul_right (by rw [mul_comm k n]; exact hWc) hn
  obtain ⟨W2, hsub, hcard⟩ := Finset.exists_superset_card_eq hWk (by simpa using hk)
  refine ⟨W2, hcard, fun ℓ hℓ G hG => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨i, hi, hle⟩ := hW ℓ hℓ G (Finset.subset_univ _) hG
  exact ⟨i, hi, hle.trans (Finset.card_le_card (Finset.inter_subset_inter_left hsub))⟩
declarations.citation: Justified Representation in Approval-Based Committee Voting (arXiv:1407.8269), theorem that PAV satisfies EJR; recalled in arXiv:2007.01795; the one-size-at-a-time part of the committee-monotonicity question

declarations.name: karp_reducible_refl
declarations.informal: Every language L over a finite alphabet Γ Karp-reduces to itself: the reduction is the identity function on words, which is computed by the identity Turing machine in a constant number of steps, and w ∈ L if and only if w ∈ L.
declarations.statement: theorem karp_reducible_refl {Γ : Type} [Fintype Γ] (L : Language Γ) : KarpReducible Γ Γ L L
declarations.source:
/-- Karp reducibility is reflexive: every language over a finite alphabet reduces to itself by the identity. -/
theorem karp_reducible_refl {Γ : Type} [Fintype Γ] (L : Language Γ) : KarpReducible Γ Γ L L := by
  exact ⟨id, ⟨Turing.idComputableInPolyTime id⟩, fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩
declarations.citation: Karp 1972 (reflexivity of ≤_p); Mathlib: Turing.idComputableInPolyTime
declarations.reading:
For every type Γ that is finite (the instance binder `[Fintype Γ]` says Γ carries a Fintype structure), and for every language L over Γ (L : Language Γ, i.e. a set of words/lists over Γ, so `w ∈ L` means w : List Γ lies in L), it is asserted that L Karp-reduces to itself, `KarpReducible Γ Γ L L`.

Unfolding the conclusion literally, the assertion is: there exists a function f : List Γ → List Γ such that

(a) `Nonempty (Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime (id : List Γ → List Γ) (id : List Γ → List Γ) f)` — i.e. f is computable by a two-tape Turing machine (the TM2 model) in polynomial time, where both the input encoding and the output encoding are the identity function on `List Γ`; and

(b) for every w : List Γ, `w ∈ L ↔ f w ∈ L`.

Quantifier order and binder structure, explicitly: `∀ Γ (Fintype Γ) (L : Language Γ), ∃ f : List Γ → List Γ, (Nonempty (poly-time-TM2-computable id id f)) ∧ (∀ w : List Γ, w ∈ L ↔ f w ∈ L)`. The type Γ is the same in both argument slots of `KarpReducible`, so this is only the self-reduction (reflexivity) instance.

declarations.name: poisson_bracket_self
declarations.informal: For any scalar function f on the phase space E × E and any phase-space point qp, the Poisson bracket {f, f}(qp) vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem poisson_bracket_self {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    (f : E × E → ℝ) (qp : E × E) :
    poisson_bracket f f qp = 0
declarations.source:
/-- The Poisson bracket of any scalar function with itself is zero. -/
theorem poisson_bracket_self {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    (f : E × E → ℝ) (qp : E × E) :
    poisson_bracket f f qp = 0 := by
  unfold poisson_bracket
  rw [real_inner_comm]
  exact sub_self _
declarations.citation: Arnold, Mathematical Methods of Classical Mechanics, §38; Goldstein, Poole & Safko, Classical Mechanics (3rd ed.), §9.4
declarations.reading: For every complete real inner product space $E$, every function $f : E \times E \to \mathbb{R}$, and every point $qp \in E \times E$, the Poisson bracket of $f$ with itself evaluated at $qp$ is $0$.

declarations.name: ccz_layer_parity_repr_card_ge
declarations.informal: The Hadamard-free floor of arXiv:2610.01024 (Corollary 83): every set of nonzero parities on 3m qubits whose order-1, 2, 3 moments equal the syndrome of the layer of m >= 1 disjoint CCZ gates has at least 6m + 1 elements; so every Hadamard-free {CNOT, T} circuit for the layer uses at least 6m + 1 T gates.
declarations.statement: theorem ccz_layer_parity_repr_card_ge (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (S : Finset (Finset (Fin (3 * m)))) (hS : is_parity_repr S (ccz_layer_syndrome m)) : 6 * m + 1 ≤ S.card
declarations.source:
/-- The CCZ-layer syndrome vanishes on every set that is not of size three. -/
theorem ccz_layer_syndrome_eq_zero_of_card_ne {m : ℕ} (A : Finset (Fin (3 * m)))
    (hA : A.card ≠ 3) : ccz_layer_syndrome m A = 0 := by
  unfold ccz_layer_syndrome
  rw [if_neg]
  rintro ⟨j, rfl⟩
  apply hA
  rw [Finset.card_eq_three]
  refine ⟨_, _, _, ?_, ?_, ?_, rfl⟩ <;> simp [Fin.ext_iff]

/-- For every qubit `i` of the layer, the two other qubits `p`, `q` of its CCZ block single out
`i`: the syndrome of `{a, p, q}` is `1` exactly when `a = i`. -/
theorem ccz_layer_syndrome_partner {m : ℕ} (i : Fin (3 * m)) :
    ∃ p q : Fin (3 * m), ∀ a, ccz_layer_syndrome m {a, p, q} = if a = i then 1 else 0 := by
  have hi := i.isLt
  refine ⟨⟨3 * (i.val / 3) + (i.val % 3 + 1) % 3, by omega⟩,
    ⟨3 * (i.val / 3) + (i.val % 3 + 2) % 3, by omega⟩, fun a => ?_⟩
  unfold ccz_layer_syndrome
  by_cases hai : a = i
  · subst hai
    rw [if_pos rfl, if_pos]
    refine ⟨⟨a.val / 3, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
    ext x
    simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff]
    omega
  · rw [if_neg hai, if_neg]
    rintro ⟨j, hj⟩
    have h1 : a ∈ ({a, ⟨3 * (i.val / 3) + (i.val % 3 + 1) % 3, by omega⟩,
        ⟨3 * (i.val / 3) + (i.val % 3 + 2) % 3, by omega⟩} : Finset (Fin (3 * m))) := by simp
    have h2 : (⟨3 * (i.val / 3) + (i.val % 3 + 1) % 3, by omega⟩ : Fin (3 * m)) ∈
        ({a, ⟨3 * (i.val / 3) + (i.val % 3 + 1) % 3, by omega⟩,
        ⟨3 * (i.val / 3) + (i.val % 3 + 2) % 3, by omega⟩} : Finset (Fin (3 * m))) := by simp
    have h3 : (⟨3 * j.val, by omega⟩ : Fin (3 * m)) ∈
        ({⟨3 * j.val, by omega⟩, ⟨3 * j.val + 1, by omega⟩, ⟨3 * j.val + 2, by omega⟩} :
          Finset (Fin (3 * m))) := by simp
    have h4 : (⟨3 * j.val + 1, by omega⟩ : Fin (3 * m)) ∈
        ({⟨3 * j.val, by omega⟩, ⟨3 * j.val + 1, by omega⟩, ⟨3 * j.val + 2, by omega⟩} :
          Finset (Fin (3 * m))) := by simp
    have h5 : (⟨3 * j.val + 2, by omega⟩ : Fin (3 * m)) ∈
        ({⟨3 * j.val, by omega⟩, ⟨3 * j.val + 1, by omega⟩, ⟨3 * j.val + 2, by omega⟩} :
          Finset (Fin (3 * m))) := by simp
    rw [hj] at h1 h2
    rw [← hj] at h3 h4 h5
    simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff] at h1 h2 h3 h4 h5
    have := Fin.val_ne_of_ne hai
    omega

theorem ccz_layer_parity_repr_card_ge (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (S : Finset (Finset (Fin (3 * m)))) (hS : is_parity_repr S (ccz_layer_syndrome m)) : 6 * m + 1 ≤ S.card := by
  classical
  -- the incidence matrix of qubits against parities
  let M : Matrix (Fin (3 * m)) S (ZMod 2) := Matrix.of fun a y => if a ∈ (y : Finset _) then 1 else 0
  have hcount : ∀ A : Finset (Fin (3 * m)),
      ((S.filter fun y => A ⊆ y).card : ZMod 2) = ∑ y : S, ∏ a ∈ A, M a y := by
    intro A
    simp only [M, Matrix.of_apply, Finset.prod_boole]
    rw [Finset.natCast_card_filter, ← Finset.sum_coe_sort S]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun y _ => ?_
    split_ifs <;> simp_all [Finset.subset_iff]
  have hsyn : ∀ A : Finset (Fin (3 * m)), A.Nonempty → A.card ≤ 3 →
      ∑ y : S, ∏ a ∈ A, M a y = ccz_layer_syndrome m A := by
    intro A hA hA3
    rw [← hcount]
    exact hS.2 A ⟨hA.card_pos, hA3⟩
  have hM01 : ∀ a y, M a y * M a y = M a y := by
    intro a y; simp only [M, Matrix.of_apply]; split_ifs <;> simp
  -- order-one and order-two moments vanish
  have h1 : ∀ a, ∑ y : S, M a y = 0 := by
    intro a
    have := hsyn {a} (by simp) (by simp)
    rw [ccz_layer_syndrome_eq_zero_of_card_ne _ (by simp)] at this
    simpa using this
  have h2 : ∀ a b, ∑ y : S, M a y * M b y = 0 := by
    intro a b
    by_cases hab : a = b
    · subst hab; simp only [hM01]; exact h1 a
    · have := hsyn {a, b} (by simp) ((Finset.card_le_two).trans (by norm_num))
      rw [ccz_layer_syndrome_eq_zero_of_card_ne _ (by rw [Finset.card_pair hab]; norm_num)] at this
      simpa only [Finset.prod_pair hab] using this
  have h3 : ∀ a b c, ∑ y : S, M a y * M b y * M c y = ccz_layer_syndrome m {a, b, c} := by
    intro a b c
    rw [← hsyn {a, b, c} (by simp) Finset.card_le_three]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun y _ => ?_
    simp only [M, Matrix.of_apply, Finset.prod_boole,
      Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, forall_eq_or_imp, forall_eq]
    split_ifs <;> simp_all
  -- S is nonempty: the first CCZ triple has odd moment
  have hne : Nonempty S := by
    by_contra hS0
    rw [not_nonempty_iff] at hS0
    have := h3 ⟨0, by omega⟩ ⟨1, by omega⟩ ⟨2, by omega⟩
    rw [Finset.univ_eq_empty, Finset.sum_empty] at this
    unfold ccz_layer_syndrome at this
    rw [if_pos ⟨⟨0, by omega⟩, by simp⟩] at this
    exact zero_ne_one this
  -- the map (v, λ) ↦ M.transpose v + λ · 1
  let L : (Fin (3 * m) → ZMod 2) × ZMod 2 →ₗ[ZMod 2] (S → ZMod 2) :=
    (Matrix.mulVecLin M.transpose).coprod (LinearMap.smulRight LinearMap.id 1)
  have hL : ∀ v l y, L (v, l) y = (∑ a, M a y * v a) + l := by
    intro v l y
    simp [L, Matrix.vecMul, dotProduct, mul_comm]
  -- evaluating against the two partners of `i` recovers `v i`
  have heval : ∀ v l i, ∃ p q : Fin (3 * m), ∑ y : S, L (v, l) y * M p y * M q y = v i := by
    intro v l i
    obtain ⟨p, q, hpq⟩ := ccz_layer_syndrome_partner i
    refine ⟨p, q, ?_⟩
    simp only [hL, add_mul, Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_mul]
    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    have e1 : ∀ a, ∑ y : S, M a y * v a * M p y * M q y = v a * ccz_layer_syndrome m {a, p, q} := by
      intro a
      rw [← h3, Finset.mul_sum]
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun y _ => by ring
    have e2 : ∑ y : S, l * M p y * M q y = 0 := by
      rw [← mul_zero l, ← h2 p q, Finset.mul_sum]
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun y _ => by ring
    simp only [e1, e2, hpq, mul_ite, mul_one, mul_zero, Finset.sum_ite_eq', Finset.mem_univ,
      if_true, add_zero]
  have hLinj : Function.Injective L := by
    rw [← LinearMap.ker_eq_bot, LinearMap.ker_eq_bot']
    rintro ⟨v, l⟩ hvl
    have hv : v = 0 := by
      funext i
      obtain ⟨p, q, h⟩ := heval v l i
      rw [← h, hvl]
      simp
    subst hv
    obtain ⟨y⟩ := hne
    have := congrFun hvl y
    rw [hL] at this
    simp only [Pi.zero_apply, mul_zero, Finset.sum_const_zero, zero_add] at this
    rw [this]; rfl
  -- the image of L lies in the kernel of M
  have hker : LinearMap.range L ≤ LinearMap.ker M.mulVecLin := by
    rintro x ⟨⟨v, l⟩, rfl⟩
    rw [LinearMap.mem_ker]
    funext b
    simp only [Matrix.mulVecLin_apply, Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, hL, Pi.zero_apply, mul_add,
      Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.mul_sum]
    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    have e1 : ∀ a, ∑ y : S, M b y * (M a y * v a) = 0 := by
      intro a
      rw [← zero_mul (v a), ← h2 b a, Finset.sum_mul]
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun y _ => by ring
    have e2 : ∑ y : S, M b y * l = 0 := by rw [← Finset.sum_mul, h1, zero_mul]
    simp only [e1, e2, Finset.sum_const_zero, add_zero]
  -- dimension count
  have hrankT : M.transpose.rank = 3 * m := by
    have hinj : Function.Injective (Matrix.mulVecLin M.transpose) := by
      intro v w hvw
      have := @hLinj (v, 0) (w, 0) (by simpa [L] using hvw)
      exact (Prod.ext_iff.1 this).1
    rw [Matrix.rank, LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj hinj, Module.finrank_fin_fun]
  have hrank : M.rank = 3 * m := by rw [← Matrix.rank_transpose]; exact hrankT
  have hnull := LinearMap.finrank_range_add_finrank_ker M.mulVecLin
  have hmono := Submodule.finrank_mono hker
  rw [LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj hLinj, Module.finrank_prod, Module.finrank_fin_fun,
    Module.finrank_self] at hmono
  rw [← Matrix.rank, hrank, Module.finrank_fintype_fun_eq_card, Fintype.card_coe] at hnull
  omega
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.01024, Corollary 83 (Hadamard-free floor of 6m + 1 for m disjoint CCZ gates)

declarations.name: is_regular_one
declarations.informal: The language {[]} containing only the empty word is regular.
declarations.statement: theorem is_regular_one {α : Type*} : (1 : Language α).IsRegular
declarations.source:
/-- The language containing only the empty word (the unit language 1) is regular. -/
theorem is_regular_one {α : Type*} : (1 : Language α).IsRegular := by
  have hfold : ∀ (y : List α) (s : Bool),
      List.foldl (fun (_ : Bool) (_ : α) => false) s y = if y = [] then s else false := by
    intro y
    induction y with
    | nil => intro s; simp
    | cons b y ih =>
      intro s
      simp only [List.foldl_cons, ih, reduceCtorEq, if_false]
      split_ifs <;> rfl
  refine ⟨Bool, inferInstance, ⟨fun _ _ => false, true, {true}⟩, ?_⟩
  ext x
  rw [DFA.mem_accepts, Language.mem_one]
  show List.foldl (fun (_ : Bool) (_ : α) => false) true x ∈ ({true} : Set Bool) ↔ x = []
  rw [hfold]
  split_ifs with h <;> simp [h]
declarations.citation: standard textbook result (automata theory): {ε} is regular

declarations.name: is_regular_pow
declarations.informal: For any regular language L and natural number n, the n-th power L^n is regular.
declarations.statement: theorem is_regular_pow {α : Type*} {L : Language α} (h : L.IsRegular) (n : ℕ) : (L ^ n).IsRegular
declarations.source:
/-- Any power of a regular language is regular. -/
theorem is_regular_pow {α : Type*} {L : Language α} (h : L.IsRegular) (n : ℕ) : (L ^ n).IsRegular := by
  induction n with
  | zero => rw [pow_zero]; exact is_regular_one
  | succ n ih => rw [pow_succ]; exact is_regular_mul ih h
declarations.citation: Sipser, Exercise 1.31
declarations.reading: For any type `α` and any formal language `L` over alphabet `α` (`L : Language α`, i.e., a set of lists of elements of `α`), if `L` is regular (`L.IsRegular`), then for every natural number `n`, the `n`-th power `L ^ n` (the language formed by the concatenation of `n` words from `L`, with `L ^ 0 = {[]}`) is also regular.

open.name: catch_up_outcome_neg_eq_loss_iff
open.informal: Negating a Catch-Up outcome yields a loss if and only if the original outcome is a win.
open.statement:
theorem catch_up_outcome_neg_eq_loss_iff (o : CatchUpOutcome) :
    o.neg = CatchUpOutcome.loss ↔ o = CatchUpOutcome.win
open.citation: folklore

open.name: catch_up_value_aux_empty_eq_draw_iff
open.informal: In a Catch-Up position with an empty set of remaining pieces, the game value for the mover is CatchUpOutcome.draw if and only if the mover's score equals the opponent's score.
open.statement:
theorem catch_up_value_aux_empty_eq_draw_iff (s_me s_opp : ℕ) (isFirstMove : Bool) :
    catch_up_value_aux ∅ s_me s_opp isFirstMove = CatchUpOutcome.draw ↔ s_me = s_opp
open.citation: Catch-Up: A Game in Which the Lead Alternates (2015)

open.name: catch_up_value_aux_icc_after_opening_lt_ne_loss
open.informal: In Catch-Up played on {1, ..., N} with N(N+1)/2 even, Player 2 does not lose after any opening move x < N by Player 1.
open.statement:
theorem catch_up_value_aux_icc_after_opening_lt_ne_loss (N : ℕ) (h_even : Even (N * (N + 1) / 2))
    (x : ℕ) (hx : x ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N) (hlt : x < N) :
    catch_up_value_aux ((Finset.Icc 1 N).erase x) 0 x false ≠ CatchUpOutcome.loss
open.citation: step towards catch_up_value_aux_icc_after_opening_ne_loss (Catch-Up conjecture (Catch-Up: A Game in Which the Lead Alternates, 2015, Sec. 3.1))

open.name: catch_up_value_aux_icc_after_opening_max_ne_loss
open.informal: In Catch-Up played on {1, ..., N} with N(N+1)/2 even and N > 0, Player 2 does not lose after Player 1 opens with the maximum piece N.
open.statement:
theorem catch_up_value_aux_icc_after_opening_max_ne_loss (N : ℕ) (h_even : Even (N * (N + 1) / 2))
    (hN : 0 < N) :
    catch_up_value_aux ((Finset.Icc 1 N).erase N) 0 N false ≠ CatchUpOutcome.loss
open.citation: step towards catch_up_value_aux_icc_after_opening_ne_loss (Catch-Up conjecture (Catch-Up: A Game in Which the Lead Alternates, 2015, Sec. 3.1))

open.name: catch_up_value_aux_icc_after_opening_ne_loss
open.informal: In Catch-Up played on {1, ..., N} with N(N+1)/2 even, Player 2 does not lose after any opening move x ∈ {1, ..., N} by Player 1.

open.name: catch_up_value_aux_icc_initial_ne_loss
open.informal: In Catch-Up played on {1, ..., N} with N(N+1)/2 even, Player 1 does not lose from the initial position with equal scores 0.

open.name: catch_up_value_aux_icc_opening_one_response_lt_ne_loss
open.informal: In Catch-Up on {1, ..., N} with even triangular sum, if Player 1 opens with 1 and Player 2 responds with y < N, Player 1 does not lose from the resulting position with scores (1, y).

theorem catch_up_value_aux_icc_opening_one_response_lt_ne_loss (N : ℕ)

open.name: catch_up_value_eq_loss_iff
open.informal: For any nonempty finite set S of natural numbers, the game value catch_up_value S is CatchUpOutcome.loss if and only if for every element x ∈ S, the second player wins from the resulting position, i.e., catch_up_value_aux (S.erase x) 0 x false = CatchUpOutcome.win.
open.statement:
theorem catch_up_value_eq_loss_iff (S : Finset ℕ) (hS : S.Nonempty) :
    catch_up_value S = CatchUpOutcome.loss ↔
      ∀ x ∈ S, catch_up_value_aux (S.erase x) 0 x false = CatchUpOutcome.win
open.citation: Catch-Up: A Game in Which the Lead Alternates (2015)

open.name: catch_up_value_icc_eq_draw_of_even_triangular
open.informal: The Catch-Up conjecture (2015, open): for every natural number N such that the triangular number N(N+1)/2 is even, the game Catch-Up played on {1, ..., N} ends in a draw under optimal play by both players. Verified by computer up to N = 20.
open.statement:
theorem catch_up_value_icc_eq_draw_of_even_triangular (N : ℕ) (h_even : Even (N * (N + 1) / 2)) :
    catch_up_value (Finset.Icc 1 N) = .draw
open.citation: Catch-Up: A Game in Which the Lead Alternates (2015)

open.name: maxcut_game_optimal_strong_equilibrium_exists
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2610.04948, Sec. 4, second question): for every finite simple unweighted graph G and every k ≥ 3, some optimal coloring of the Max-k-Cut game on (G, k) is a strong equilibrium. This would imply that every such game has a strong equilibrium.
open.statement:
theorem maxcut_game_optimal_strong_equilibrium_exists :
    ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k : ℕ),
      3 ≤ k → ∃ σ : V → Fin k, is_maxcut_optimal G σ ∧ is_maxcut_strong_equilibrium G σ
open.citation: second open question of arXiv:2610.04948, Sec. 4 (does every game admit an optimal coloring that is a strong equilibrium?); the paper's Theorem 2 shows not every optimal coloring is one, and Remark 6 notes its counterexample does not rule out another, stable optimum

open.name: maxcut_game_strong_equilibrium_exists
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2610.04948, Sec. 4): for every finite simple unweighted graph G and every k ≥ 3, the unweighted Max-k-Cut game on (G, k) has a strong equilibrium, i.e. a coloring σ : V → [k] from which no nonempty coalition can deviate so that every member strictly gains.
open.statement:
theorem maxcut_game_strong_equilibrium_exists :
    ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k : ℕ),
      3 ≤ k → ∃ σ : V → Fin k, is_maxcut_strong_equilibrium G σ
open.citation: open question of arXiv:2610.04948, Sec. 4 (Concluding remarks); that paper shows an optimal coloring need not be a strong equilibrium (Theorem 2), which leaves existence open; known: optimal colorings are strong equilibria when the maximum degree is at most 2k − 1 (Corollary 9) and are 7-strong equilibria in general

open.name: maxcut_optimal_not_strong_degree_66
open.informal: There is a finite simple graph of maximum degree at most 66 with an optimal coloring of the Max-3-Cut game that is not a strong equilibrium; hence Δ*(3) ≤ 65. (The graph G_3 of arXiv:2610.04948, Sec. 2, has 91 vertices and maximum degree 66, attained by the anchor vertices r_{3,1}.)
open.statement: theorem maxcut_optimal_not_strong_degree_66 : ¬ maxcut_optimal_strong_up_to_degree 3 66
open.citation: arXiv:2610.04948, Theorem 2 for k = 3, with the degree bound read off the construction G_3 of Sec. 2.1 (the paper does not state the degree); the upper bound side of the threshold question after Corollary 9

open.name: mms_threshold_monotone_asymptotic
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2610.06125, Sec. 3): for monotone valuations over goods, μ(n) = n + log₂ n + o(log₂ n) as n → ∞; i.e. (μ(n) − n − log₂ n) / log₂ n → 0.
open.statement:
theorem mms_threshold_monotone_asymptotic :
    (fun n : ℕ => (mms_threshold_monotone n : ℝ) - n - Real.logb 2 n) =o[Filter.atTop]
      (fun n : ℕ => Real.logb 2 n)
open.citation: open question of arXiv:2610.06125 (On MMS allocations with few items), Sec. 3; the paper proves n + 0.93 log₂ n ≤ μ(n) ≤ n + log₂ n + O(log log n) for large n (Theorem 1, Theorem 6, Lemmas 8 and 9)

open.name: condorcet_dimension_le_three
open.informal: Open problem: every election with at least one voter has a Condorcet winning set of at most three candidates, i.e. the Condorcet dimension of every election is at most 3.
open.statement:
theorem condorcet_dimension_le_three :
    ∀ (n m : ℕ) (P : Fin n → Equiv.Perm (Fin m)), 0 < n →
      ∃ S : Finset (Fin m), S.card ≤ 3 ∧ is_condorcet_winning_set P S
open.citation: open question from Condorcet winning sets (Social Choice and Welfare 44(3):493-517, 2015); dimension 3 is attained, and the best upper bound is 5 (arXiv:2506.22133); arXiv:2604.19851 finds no election of dimension above 3 by computer search

open.name: ejr_committee_monotone_chain_exists
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2007.01795, open problems, Q2): every approval profile with at least one voter admits an ordering c_1, ..., c_m of all candidates such that for every k ≤ m the prefix {c_1, ..., c_k} satisfies EJR for committee size k; equivalently, some resolute committee-monotonic approval-based committee rule satisfies EJR.
open.statement:
theorem ejr_committee_monotone_chain_exists :
    ∀ (n m : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Finset (Fin m)), 0 < n →
      ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin m), ∀ k, k ≤ m →
        is_ejr_committee A k (Finset.univ.filter fun c => (σ c : ℕ) < k)
open.citation: open question of arXiv:2007.01795 (Multi-Winner Voting with Approval Preferences) (committee monotonicity and proportionality); sequential Phragmén is committee monotonic but only satisfies PJR, and the known EJR rules are not committee monotonic; a positive answer is known for party-list profiles (arXiv:1911.08365)

open.name: crystal_components_unique
open.informal: Crystals have unique components (arXiv:1601.03081, open): if n is a crystal with components a, b and also with components c, d, then {a, b} = {c, d}.
open.citation: The Biharmonic Mean (2016), arXiv:1601.03081

open.name: weakly_consecutive_one_at_end
open.informal: Conjecture 5.2 of arXiv:2401.09497 (open): every weakly consecutive sequence of length k begins or ends with the term 1, that is, the position holding the value 1 is the first or the last.
open.statement:
theorem weakly_consecutive_one_at_end {k : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin k))
    (hσ : is_weakly_consecutive σ) (i : Fin k) (hi : (σ i : ℕ) = 0) :
    (i : ℕ) = 0 ∨ (i : ℕ) + 1 = k
open.citation: Weakly Consecutive Sequences (2024), arXiv:2401.09497

open.name: matrix3_tensor_rank_int_le_22
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2610.01639, Sec. 8): there is a bilinear algorithm for 3x3 matrix multiplication with integer coefficients that uses 22 products, i.e. a list of 22 triads over the integers whose evaluation equals A * B for all integer 3x3 matrices A and B. By the paper, such an algorithm is the same as a recursive (block) algorithm with integer constants and 22 multiplications; the paper proves at least 22 are needed and 23 suffice, so the question is whether the rank is exactly 22.
open.statement: theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_int_le_22 : matrix3_tensor_rank_le ℤ 22
open.citation: the open problem of arXiv:2610.01639, Sec. 8 (a 22-product integer algorithm for 3x3 matrix multiplication), stated as posed

open.name: matrix3_tensor_rank_z_ge_22
open.informal: The tensor rank of 3x3 matrix multiplication over the integers is at least 22; that is, every valid decomposition of 3x3 matrix multiplication over ℤ has length at least 22.
open.statement: theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_z_ge_22 : matrix3_tensor_rank_ge ℤ 22
open.citation: arXiv:2610.01639, Theorem 1 and Sec. 8 (Lower Bound of 22 for 3x3 Matrix Multiplication over the Integers)

open.name: matrix3_tensor_rank_zmod2_ge_22
open.informal: Every bilinear algorithm (valid triad decomposition) for 3x3 matrix multiplication over the two-element field uses at least 22 products. This is the main lower bound of arXiv:2610.01639 (row 0 of its table), proved there by a large computer-assisted Lean development.
open.statement: theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_zmod2_ge_22 : matrix3_tensor_rank_ge (ZMod 2) 22
open.citation: arXiv:2610.01639, Sec. 3 and Sec. 7, Table 1, row 0: the paper's main lower bound of 22 over the two-element field

open.name: matrix3_tensor_rank_zmod2_le_22
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2610.01639, Sec. 7, Table 1, row 0, interval [22, 23]): the tensor rank of 3x3 matrix multiplication over the two-element field is 22, i.e. there are 22 triads over ZMod 2 whose evaluation equals A * B for all 3x3 matrices A, B over ZMod 2. The paper proves the rank is at least 22 and at most 23.
open.statement: theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_zmod2_le_22 : matrix3_tensor_rank_le (ZMod 2) 22
open.citation: the open problem of arXiv:2610.01639, Sec. 7, Table 1, row 0 (rank over the two-element field in [22, 23]), stated as posed

open.name: graph_matching_num_two_mul_le_card
open.informal: In any finite simple graph G on vertex set V, twice the matching number is at most the number of vertices, 2 * graph_matching_num G ≤ |V|.
open.statement:
theorem graph_matching_num_two_mul_le_card {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    2 * graph_matching_num G ≤ (Fintype.card V : ℕ∞)
open.citation: folklore

open.name: konig_matching_vertex_cover_num
open.informal: König's theorem: in any finite bipartite simple graph G, the matching number is equal to the vertex cover number.
open.statement:
theorem konig_matching_vertex_cover_num {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (h : G.IsBipartite) :
    graph_matching_num G = G.vertexCoverNum
open.citation: Diestel, Graph Theory, Theorem 2.1.1

open.name: temporal_path_snapshots_explore_n_log_n
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2610.06228, Sec. 7): temporal graphs whose snapshots are all spanning paths can always be explored in O(n log n) steps; i.e. there is a constant C such that every such temporal graph on n ≥ 2 vertices can be explored from any start vertex within C·n·log n time steps. (A disproof shows that the exploration time can exceed Θ(n log n).)
open.statement:
theorem temporal_path_snapshots_explore_n_log_n :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → ∀ G : ℕ → SimpleGraph (Fin n), (∀ t, is_spanning_path_graph (G t)) →
      ∀ s : Fin n, ∃ (w : ℕ → Fin n) (T : ℕ), w 0 = s ∧ is_temporal_walk G w ∧
        temporal_walk_explores_by w T ∧ (T : ℝ) ≤ C * n * Real.log n
open.citation: open question of arXiv:2610.06228 (Hiding a Vertex from the Temporal Explorer), Sec. 7 ('The role of the hub'): the best known lower bound for path snapshots is Ω(n log n) and it is unknown whether it can be improved; the general upper bound is O(n²)

open.name: resolution_fpt_incidence_treewidth
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2610.02047, abstract and Sec. 8): every unsatisfiable CNF formula has an FPT-sized resolution refutation parameterized by incidence treewidth; that is, there are a computable g : N -> N and a constant c >= 1 such that every unsatisfiable CNF formula F with n variables and m clauses has a resolution refutation (initial clauses, weakening, resolution) of length at most g(tw*(F)) * (n + m)^c.
open.statement: theorem resolution_fpt_incidence_treewidth : ∃ g : ℕ → ℕ, Computable g ∧ ∃ c : ℕ, 1 ≤ c ∧ ∀ F : Finset (Finset (CnfLit ℕ)), ¬ CnfSatisfiable (F.toList.map Finset.toList) → ∃ π, is_resolution_refutation F π ∧ π.length ≤ g (cnf_incidence_treewidth F) * ((cnf_vars F).card + F.card) ^ c
open.citation: the open problem of arXiv:2610.02047, abstract and Sec. 8 (FPT-sized resolution refutations parameterized by incidence treewidth), stated as posed

open.name: ccz_layer_t_count_below_6m_plus_1_with_hadamards
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2610.01024, abstract and Sec. 1): in general Clifford+T circuits, with Hadamards anywhere and any number of clean ancillas, some layer of m >= 2 disjoint CCZ gates can be implemented with strictly fewer than 6m + 1 T gates (the exact count 6m + 1 is proved only for Hadamard-free circuits).
open.statement: theorem ccz_layer_t_count_below_6m_plus_1_with_hadamards : ∃ m : ℕ, 2 ≤ m ∧ ∃ (a : ℕ) (gs : List (CliffordTGate (3 * m + a))), implements_ccz_layer m a gs ∧ clifford_t_circuit_t_count gs < 6 * m + 1
open.citation: the open problem of arXiv:2610.01024, abstract and Sec. 1 (fewer than 6m + 1 T gates with Hadamards and ancillas), stated as posed; related: its Corollary 83

open.name: gf8_oracle_t_count_ge_20
open.informal: The slice-rank floor of arXiv:2610.01024 Proposition 59 at k = 3: every parity representation of the GF(8) multiplication oracle's syndrome has at least G(3) = 20 parities (every nonzero slice of the multiplication tensor has rank 6, so the column code is an even self-orthogonal [t, 9, 8] code, and the Griesmer bound gives t >= 20).
open.statement: theorem gf8_oracle_t_count_ge_20 (S : Finset (Finset (Fin 9))) (hS : is_parity_repr S gf8_oracle_syndrome) : 20 ≤ S.card
open.citation: arXiv:2610.01024, Proposition 59 (slice-rank floor), special case k = 3

open.name: gf8_oracle_t_count_ge_24
open.informal: Negation of the premise of Open Problem 10 of arXiv:2610.01024: every set of nonzero parities on nine qubits whose order-1, 2, 3 moments equal the syndrome of the GF(8) multiplication oracle has at least 24 elements, i.e. delta(U_3) > 23, so the T-count is none of 20, 21, 22, 23. Evidence (not a Lean proof): a SAT encoding of the moment equations, which reproduces the known values 7 (CCZ), 17 (GF(4)) and 2n + 1 for the line cubic with n = 5..8, is unsatisfiable for every size up to 26 and satisfiable at 29.
open.statement: theorem gf8_oracle_t_count_ge_24 (S : Finset (Finset (Fin 9))) (hS : is_parity_repr S gf8_oracle_syndrome) : 24 ≤ S.card
open.citation: would refute the premise of Open Problem 10 of arXiv:2610.01024 (T-count in [20, 23]); related: its Proposition 59 floor of 20

open.name: gf8_oracle_t_count_le_23
open.informal: Open Problem 10 of arXiv:2610.01024 presupposes that the T-count delta(U_3) of the GF(8) multiplication oracle (Hadamard-free {CNOT, T} circuits, diagonal Cliffords free) lies in [20, 23] and asks for its value: this is the upper end, that some set of at most 23 nonzero parities on nine qubits has order-1, 2, 3 moments equal to the oracle's syndrome. A SAT search run on 2026-10-05 found no such set of size at most 26 (not a Lean proof).
open.statement: theorem gf8_oracle_t_count_le_23 : ∃ S : Finset (Finset (Fin 9)), is_parity_repr S gf8_oracle_syndrome ∧ S.card ≤ 23
open.citation: the premise of Open Problem 10 of arXiv:2610.01024 (T-count of the GF(8) multiplication oracle in [20, 23]), upper end, stated as posed

open.name: open_problem_line_cubic_t_count
open.informal: For every integer n ≥ 5, there exists a parity representation of the line cubic syndrome of cardinality 2n + 1.
open.statement: theorem open_problem_line_cubic_t_count (n : ℕ) (hn : 5 ≤ n) : ∃ S : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), is_parity_repr S (line_syndrome n) ∧ S.card = 2 * n + 1
open.citation: arXiv:2610.01024, Appendix K.2, item 1

literature.title: Existence of a 22-multiplication algorithm for 3x3 matrix multiplication over ℤ
literature.statement: Does there exist an algorithm for 3x3 matrix multiplication with integer constants that can be applied recursively (or equivalently, a bilinear decomposition of the 3x3 matrix multiplication tensor over ℤ) using 22 multiplications, or is 23 multiplications the minimum?
literature.source_title: Lower Bound of 22 for 3x3 Matrix Multiplication over the Integers
literature.rationale: The authors prove a lower bound of 22 multiplications for any recursive 3x3 algorithm with integer constants, improving the previous bound of 21. Laderman's 1976 algorithm provides an upper bound of 23. Whether 22 is achievable over the integers remains unresolved.

literature.title: Tensor rank of 3x3 matrix multiplication over F2
literature.statement: Is the tensor rank of 3x3 matrix multiplication over the finite field F2 equal to 22 or 23? That is, does there exist a set of 22 triad products whose F2-linear combinations compute the product of two arbitrary 3x3 matrices over F2, or is the rank at least 23?
literature.source_title: Lower Bound of 22 for 3x3 Matrix Multiplication over the Integers
literature.rationale: The paper proves in Lean that the tensor rank of 3x3 matrix multiplication over F2 is at least 22 (class 495 in Wang's table), improving on the lower bound of 21 from Wang (2026) and Yang et al. (2026). Laderman's 1976 decomposition yields an upper bound of 23 over F2. Thus the exact rank over F2 is either 22 or 23, leaving a gap of exactly one.

literature.title: T-count of parallel CCZ gates in general Clifford+T with Hadamards
literature.statement: Let m ≥ 2 be an integer, and let U_m = ⨂_{j=1}^m CCZ_{3j-2, 3j-1, 3j} be the unitary operator on 3m qubits that acts as the three-qubit Controlled-Controlled-Z gate CCZ = diag(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, -1) on each disjoint triplet of qubits (3j-2, 3j-1, 3j). In a general Clifford+T quantum circuit with an arbitrary number a ≥ 0 of clean ancilla qubits (initialized and returned to |0⟩), where gates may be arbitrary single-qubit Hadamards H, phase gates S = diag(1, i), CNOT gates, and T = diag(1, e^{iπ/4}) gates: can U_m be implemented using strictly fewer than 6m + 1 gates of type T?
literature.source_title: Exact $T$-counts of Toffoli layers from an isotropy bound
literature.rationale: The paper proves that every Hadamard-free Clifford+T circuit with clean ancillas implementing m disjoint CCZ gates requires at least 6m+1 T gates, which matches the Campbell-Howard construction. However, general Clifford+T circuits may place Hadamard gates freely between T gates. For m = 1, it is known that CCZ requires 7 T gates even with Hadamards, but for m ≥ 2 it is unknown whether intermediate Hadamard gates can reduce the T-count below 6m+1.

literature.title: Exact T-count of the line cubic phase gate family
literature.statement: For an integer n ≥ 5, let f_n : (ZMod 2)^n → ZMod 2 be the cubic form f_n(x_1, ..., x_n) = ∑_{i=1}^{n-2} x_i x_{i+1} x_{i+2}, and let U_{f_n} be the diagonal n-qubit gate acting by |x⟩ ↦ (-1)^{f_n(x)} |x⟩. Let δ(U_{f_n}) denote the minimum number of T gates required to implement U_{f_n} in a Hadamard-free {CNOT, T} circuit with diagonal Clifford gates free. By Proposition 65, δ(U_{f_n}) ≥ 2n + 1 for all n ≥ 5, with equality δ(U_{f_n}) = 2n + 1 known to hold for 5 ≤ n ≤ 12. Does δ(U_{f_n}) = 2n + 1 hold for all n ≥ 5?
literature.source_title: Exact $T$-counts of Toffoli layers from an isotropy bound

literature.title: Exact T-count of the GF(8) multiplication oracle
literature.statement: Let U_3 be the reversible multiplication oracle for the finite field GF(8) = GF(2^3) acting on 9 qubits by |a, b, c⟩ ↦ |a, b, c ⊕ (a · b)⟩ for a, b, c ∈ GF(8). Under Clifford equivalence to a diagonal level-three gate, its T-count δ(U_3) in Hadamard-free {CNOT, T} circuits with clean ancillas is known to satisfy 20 ≤ δ(U_3) ≤ 23, where 20 is the slice-rank lower bound (Proposition 59) and 23 is achieved by known compiled circuits. What is the exact T-count δ(U_3) of the GF(8) oracle? Specifically, is it 20, 23, or an intermediate value (21 or 22)?
literature.source_title: Exact $T$-counts of Toffoli layers from an isotropy bound

literature.title: FPT-sized resolution refutations parameterized by incidence treewidth
literature.statement: Does every unsatisfiable CNF formula have an FPT-sized resolution refutation parameterized by its incidence treewidth? Precisely: do there exist a computable function $g: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and a constant $c \ge 1$ such that for every unsatisfiable CNF formula $F$ with $n$ variables and $m$ clauses, there exists a resolution refutation of $F$ of length at most $g(\mathrm{tw}^*(F)) (n+m)^c$? Here, a CNF formula $F$ is a finite set of clauses over a finite set of Boolean variables $V$, where each clause is a finite disjunction of literals (variables or their negations); the incidence graph $G^*(F)$ is the bipartite graph with vertex set $V \cup F$ and edges $\{x, C\}$ for every variable $x \in \mathrm{var}(C)$; $\mathrm{tw}^*(F)$ is the treewidth of $G^*(F)$; and a resolution refutation is a sequence of clauses ending in $\bot$ derived by weakening and resolution.
literature.source_title: Short Resolution Refutations for CNFs with Bounded Weighted Incidence Treewidth
literature.rationale: Central open question in parameterized proof complexity, explicitly highlighted in the paper's abstract, introduction, and conclusion.

literature.title: EFX existence for four or more agents with additive goods
literature.statement: There are $n$ agents $N=\{1,\dots,n\}$ and a finite set $M$ of $m$ indivisible goods. Agent $i$ has an additive valuation $v_i(S)=\sum_{g\in S} v_i(g)$ with $v_i(g)\ge 0$. An allocation is an ordered partition $A=(A_1,\dots,A_n)$ of $M$ (every good is allocated; bundles may be empty). The allocation is EFX (envy-free up to any good) if for all agents $i\ne j$ and every good $g\in A_j$ we have $v_i(A_i)\ge v_i(A_j\setminus\{g\})$. Question: for every $n\ge 4$, every $m$ and every additive valuation profile, does an EFX allocation exist? (Some papers quantify only over $g$ with $v_i(g)>0$; for strictly positive values the two versions coincide, and both are open. The smallest open case is $n=4$.)
literature.source_title: Fair Division of Indivisible Goods: Recent Progress and Open Questions
literature.location: Sec. 4.1, Open Problem 2 (EFX itself first proposed in 'The Unreasonable Fairness of Maximum Nash Welfare', ACM TEAC 2019, DOI:10.1145/3355902, which left existence open)
literature.rationale: Widely called the central open problem of discrete fair division. Known: $n=2$ (cut-and-choose, arXiv:1707.04769); $n=3$ with additive valuations ('EFX Exists for Three Agents', arXiv:2002.05119), extended to three agents when at least one valuation is additive/MMS-feasible (arXiv:2205.07638); EFX with at most one unallocated good for $n=4$ (arXiv:2102.10654); EFX with at most $n-2$ unallocated goods in general (arXiv:2102.10654, arXiv:2107.09901); complete EFX when $m\le n+3$ and, for $n=4$, when $m\le 9$ (arXiv:2608.08590, computer-assisted); EFX for up to three valuation types ('EFX Exists for Three Types of Agents', EC 2025); EF2X for four agents (arXiv:2412.00254); EFX on multigraph instances (arXiv:2606.18665). On the negative side, EFX fails for three agents with monotone submodular valuations (arXiv:2604.18216, arXiv:2605.06451) and for $n\ge 4$ additive chores (arXiv:2606.08872), but no additive-goods counterexample is known.

literature.title: EFX for three agents with additive chores
literature.statement: There are $3$ agents and a finite set $M$ of $m$ indivisible chores. Agent $i$ has an additive cost function $c_i(S)=\sum_{e\in S}c_i(e)$ with $c_i(e)\ge 0$. An allocation is a partition $A=(A_1,A_2,A_3)$ of $M$ (all chores assigned). It is EFX for chores if for all agents $i\ne j$ and every chore $e\in A_i$, $c_i(A_i\setminus\{e\})\le c_i(A_j)$. Question: does every such 3-agent instance admit an EFX allocation? (Variant quantifying only over $e$ with $c_i(e)>0$ is equally open; with strictly positive costs they coincide.)
literature.source_title: EFX for Additive Chores: Nonexistence, Pareto Incompatibility, and Bi-Valued Existence
literature.location: Sec. 1 (introduction) and Sec. 6 (open problems); the n=3 gap is also the explicit frontier in arXiv:2609.10585
literature.rationale: After the 2026 counterexample for every $n\ge 4$ (tri-valued costs, two agent types, three chore types; arXiv:2606.08872), three agents is the only remaining number of agents for which EFX existence under additive costs is undecided (two agents is easy by cut-and-choose). Known for $n=3$: all instances with $m\le 8$ chores (arXiv:2609.10585, SMT-verified); personalized bi-valued instances; EFX together with fractional Pareto optimality for bi-valued costs; instances with $m\le 2n$; two chore types. Approximate EFX results exist (e.g. arXiv:2410.18655). A small-$n$ question with a finite search frontier ($m=9$ next), so it is a natural target for computer-assisted search and Lean-checked certificates.

literature.title: Best universal approximation ratio for maximin share with additive goods
literature.statement: There are $n$ agents $N=\{1,\dots,n\}$ and a finite set $M$ of $m$ indivisible goods. Agent $i$ has an additive valuation $v_i(S)=\sum_{g\in S} v_i(g)$ with $v_i(g)\ge 0$. An allocation is an ordered partition $A=(A_1,\dots,A_n)$ of $M$ (every good is allocated; bundles may be empty). The maximin share of agent $i$ is $\mu_i=\max_{(P_1,\dots,P_n)}\min_k v_i(P_k)$, the maximum over all partitions of $M$ into $n$ bundles. For $\alpha\in(0,1]$ an allocation is $\alpha$-MMS if $v_i(A_i)\ge\alpha\,\mu_i$ for every $i$. Let $\alpha^*$ be the supremum of $\alpha$ such that every instance (any $n$, $m$, additive $v$) admits an $\alpha$-MMS allocation. Question: determine $\alpha^*$; currently $7/9\le\alpha^*\le 20/21$.
literature.source_title: Fair Division of Indivisible Goods: Recent Progress and Open Questions
literature.rationale: Exact MMS allocations need not exist for $n\ge 3$, so the right constant is a central question. Lower bounds: $3/4+3/3836$ (arXiv:2307.07304), $10/13$ (arXiv:2510.10423), and $7/9$ with an FPTAS for $7/9-\varepsilon$ (arXiv:2511.13056). Upper bounds: $39/40$ for three agents (arXiv:2104.04977), improved to $20/21$ with four agents and eleven goods, together with an asymptotic bound $1-\Omega((\log n)^{-2})$ (arXiv:2609.15085). The gap $[0.778, 0.952]$ remains wide.

literature.title: Best universal approximation ratio for maximin share with additive chores
literature.statement: There are $n$ agents and a finite set $M$ of indivisible chores; agent $i$ has an additive cost $c_i(S)=\sum_{e\in S}c_i(e)$ with $c_i(e)\ge 0$. An allocation partitions $M$ into $(A_1,\dots,A_n)$. The maximin share (for chores) is $\mu_i=\min_{(P_1,\dots,P_n)}\max_k c_i(P_k)$ over all partitions of $M$ into $n$ bundles. For $\beta\ge 1$ an allocation is $\beta$-MMS if $c_i(A_i)\le\beta\,\mu_i$ for all $i$. Let $\beta^*$ be the infimum of $\beta$ such that every instance admits a $\beta$-MMS allocation. Question: determine $\beta^*$; currently $31/30\le\beta^*\le 13/11$.
literature.source_title: Approximation Algorithms for Max-Min Share Allocations of Indivisible Chores and Goods
literature.rationale: The chores counterpart of OP-9, introduced in arXiv:1604.01435 (which showed exact MMS can fail for chores and gave a 2-approximation). Existence bound $13/11$ through a reduction to the MultiFit job-scheduling algorithm (arXiv:2302.04581), with better bounds for small $n$ ($15/13$ for $n=3$ there; $19/18$ for three agents in arXiv:2205.05363). Impossibility $44/43$ with three agents (arXiv:2104.04977), improved to $31/30$ with four agents and eleven chores, plus asymptotic $1+\Omega((\log n)^{-2})$ (arXiv:2609.15085).

literature.title: Maximin share approximation for three agents with additive goods
literature.statement: Same model as the general MMS problem (see OP-9) with exactly $n=3$ agents: finite goods set $M$, additive $v_i\ge 0$, $\mu_i=\max$ over partitions of $M$ into 3 bundles of the minimum bundle value, and an allocation is $\alpha$-MMS if $v_i(A_i)\ge\alpha\mu_i$ for $i=1,2,3$. Let $\alpha_3^*$ be the largest $\alpha$ such that every 3-agent instance admits an $\alpha$-MMS allocation. Question: determine $\alpha_3^*$; currently $11/12\le\alpha_3^*\le 39/40$.
literature.source_title: Improved maximin fair allocation of indivisible items to three agents
literature.rationale: The smallest case where exact MMS can fail. The $11/12$ guarantee (arXiv:2205.05363) is shown best possible for a restricted kind of allocation (one prespecified agent gets her full proportional share), so improving it needs new ideas. The $39/40$ example (three agents, nine goods; arXiv:2104.04977) is proven to be the worst possible among instances with fewer than six more items than agents, so any better impossibility needs at least ten goods. With three agents the problem is small enough for computer-assisted search on the impossibility side.

literature.title: Polynomial-time computation of EF1 and Pareto-optimal allocations of goods
literature.statement: There are $n$ agents $N=\{1,\dots,n\}$ and a finite set $M$ of $m$ indivisible goods. Agent $i$ has an additive valuation $v_i(S)=\sum_{g\in S} v_i(g)$ with $v_i(g)\ge 0$. An allocation is an ordered partition $A=(A_1,\dots,A_n)$ of $M$ (every good is allocated; bundles may be empty). Values are given as nonnegative integers (or rationals) in binary. An allocation is EF1 if for all $i\ne j$ with $A_j\ne\emptyset$ there is $g\in A_j$ with $v_i(A_i)\ge v_i(A_j\setminus\{g\})$, and Pareto optimal (PO) if no allocation $B$ has $v_i(B_i)\ge v_i(A_i)$ for all $i$ with strict inequality for some $i$. An EF1+PO allocation always exists (e.g. a maximum Nash welfare allocation). Question: is there an algorithm that outputs an EF1+PO allocation in time polynomial in $n$, $m$ and the bit length of the values?
literature.source_title: Fair Division of Indivisible Goods: Recent Progress and Open Questions
literature.rationale: Existence follows from maximum Nash welfare ('The Unreasonable Fairness of Maximum Nash Welfare'), but computing that allocation is APX-hard. A market-based pseudo-polynomial algorithm finds EF1+PO (arXiv:1707.04731); polynomial time is known for a fixed number of agents (arXiv:2411.01810), for binary and other few-valued instances, and for EF1+fPO under extra structure. For chores, EF1+PO existence was settled in 2025 (arXiv:2507.09544), but only with polynomial time for constant $n$. A general polynomial algorithm, or evidence of hardness (e.g. PLS/PPAD), is open.

literature.title: EF1 and Pareto optimality for mixed goods and chores
literature.statement: There are $n$ agents and a finite set $M$ of indivisible items. Agent $i$ has an additive valuation $v_i(S)=\sum_{o\in S}v_i(o)$ with $v_i(o)\in\mathbb{R}$ of arbitrary sign (an item may be a good for one agent and a chore for another). An allocation is a partition $(A_1,\dots,A_n)$ of $M$. It is EF1 if for all $i\ne j$, either $v_i(A_i)\ge v_i(A_j)$ or there is an item $o\in A_i\cup A_j$ with $v_i(A_i\setminus\{o\})\ge v_i(A_j\setminus\{o\})$. It is Pareto optimal if no allocation $B$ has $v_i(B_i)\ge v_i(A_i)$ for all $i$ with strict inequality for some $i$. Question: does every such instance (for every $n\ge 3$) admit an allocation that is both EF1 and Pareto optimal?
literature.source_title: Fair allocation of combinations of indivisible goods and chores
literature.rationale: For goods, maximum Nash welfare gives EF1+PO; for chores, existence was proven only in 2025 by a fixed-point argument (arXiv:2507.09544). For mixed manna, EF1 alone is easy (a double round-robin) and EF1+PO is known for two agents (arXiv:1807.10684), but the general case is open, even for three agents. Partial progress: PO with introspective EF1 (arXiv:2509.18673) and PO with envy-freeness up to $n-1$ reallocations (arXiv:2507.03946). A positive answer would unify the goods and chores theories.

literature.title: Query complexity of envy-free cake cutting
literature.statement: The cake is $[0,1]$. Each of $n$ agents has a valuation $v_i$: a nonatomic probability measure on $[0,1]$ (additive, $v_i([0,1])=1$, single points have measure 0). In the Robertson–Webb query model a protocol may ask $\mathrm{Eval}_i(x,y)=v_i([x,y])$ and $\mathrm{Cut}_i(x,\alpha)=$ some $y$ with $v_i([x,y])=\alpha$. It must output an allocation: disjoint pieces $A_1,\dots,A_n$, each a finite union of intervals, covering $[0,1]$, that is envy-free ($v_i(A_i)\ge v_i(A_j)$ for all $i,j$). Let $T(n)$ be the minimum, over protocols, of the worst-case number of queries. Question: is $T(n)$ bounded by a polynomial in $n$? More generally, determine the growth of $T(n)$.
literature.source_title: A Discrete and Bounded Envy-Free Cake Cutting Protocol for Any Number of Agents
literature.rationale: Bounded protocols were found only in 2015-16: four agents (arXiv:1508.05143, improved to about 171 queries in arXiv:1807.00317) and any $n$ with a tower of exponentials (arXiv:1604.03655). A later sharper analysis gave $n^{O(n^2)}$, and a September 2026 preprint claims $n^{O(1)}2^n$ (arXiv:2609.05191; not yet peer-reviewed). The only lower bound is $\Omega(n^2)$ ('Thou Shalt Covet Thy Neighbor's Cake'). Even for $n=4$ the exact query complexity is unknown. With connected pieces, exact envy-freeness cannot be reached by any finite protocol, and the connected approximate version is a separate open question (see OP-18).

literature.title: Best approximation factor for EFX with additive goods
literature.statement: There are $n$ agents $N=\{1,\dots,n\}$ and a finite set $M$ of $m$ indivisible goods. Agent $i$ has an additive valuation $v_i(S)=\sum_{g\in S} v_i(g)$ with $v_i(g)\ge 0$. An allocation is an ordered partition $A=(A_1,\dots,A_n)$ of $M$ (every good is allocated; bundles may be empty). For $\alpha\in(0,1]$ an allocation is $\alpha$-EFX if for all $i\ne j$ and all $g\in A_j$, $v_i(A_i)\ge\alpha\,v_i(A_j\setminus\{g\})$. Let $\alpha^*$ be the supremum of $\alpha$ such that every instance (any $n$, $m$) admits an $\alpha$-EFX allocation. Currently $\varphi-1=(\sqrt5-1)/2\approx0.618\le\alpha^*\le 1$. Question: determine $\alpha^*$; in particular, does a $2/3$-EFX allocation (or any $\alpha>\varphi-1$) always exist for every $n$?
literature.source_title: Fair Division of Indivisible Goods: Recent Progress and Open Questions
