An exploration is complete when every vertex in $V$ has been visited at the start or intermediate vertex of some step. For always-connected temporal graphs on $n$ vertices with underlying maximum degree at most $\Delta$, does any lower bound on exploration time with linear (or super-constant) dependence on $\Delta$ survive? That is, does there exist a constant $c > 0$ such that for arbitrarily large $n$ and $\Delta$, some always-connected temporal graph requires $\Omega(\Delta n)$ (or $\Omega(f(\Delta) n)$ for some $f(\Delta) = \omega(1)$) time steps to explore under two moves per step, or can every such temporal graph be explored in $o(\Delta n)$ (or $O(n \log n)$) steps?

literature.title: Explicit polynomial-size robust subspace designs for all dimensions
literature.statement: For positive integers $k \le n$, an operator-norm bounded family of linear maps $Q_1, \ldots, Q_m: \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}^k$ (with $\|Q_i\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le 1$) is a $(k, \eta, \Delta)$-weak robust subspace design if for every $k$-dimensional subspace $W \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n$, at most $\Delta$ indices $i \in [m]$ satisfy $\sigma_{\min}(Q_i|_W) \le \eta$, where $\sigma_{\min}(Q_i|_W) = \inf_{w \in W, \|w\|=1} \|Q_i w\|$. Does there exist an explicit (deterministic polynomial-time or logspace-uniform) construction that, given $n$ and $1 \le k \le n$, outputs a $(k, \eta, \Delta)$-weak robust subspace design $\mathcal{Q}_{n,k} = \{Q_1, \ldots, Q_m\}$ with entries in $\mathbb{Q}(i)$ such that the size $m \le n^{c}$ and the robustness $\eta \ge n^{-c}$ for some universal constant $c > 0$, with $\Delta \le m - 1$?
literature.source_title: Robust subspace designs and the power of a unique small quantum witness
literature.rationale: The paper shows that a random family of $O(k(n-k)\log(nk))$ Gaussian matrices achieves inverse-polynomial robustness $\eta = \Theta(1/\sqrt{nk})$ with high probability. However, its explicit deterministic construction based on sketching and coordinate projections has size $O(n^4 k^{O(k)})$, which is polynomial only when $k = O(\log n / \log \log n)$. Derandomizing this to an explicit polynomial-size construction for all $1 \le k \le n$ would derandomize quantum witness isolation from randomized logspace to deterministic logspace.

literature.title: Truthful polynomial-communication mechanism beating 1/2 for two XOS valuations
literature.statement: Consider a two-bidder combinatorial auction on a set $M$ of $m$ items, where each bidder $i \in \{1, 2\}$ has an XOS valuation $v_i : 2^M \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, meaning $v_i(S) = \max_{k \in K_i} \sum_{e \in S} a_{k, e}^{(i)}$ for a finite collection of nonnegative additive supporting clauses $a_k^{(i)}$. Does there exist a constant $\varepsilon > 0$ and an individually rational, no-negative-transfers truthful (ex-post Nash or dominant-strategy incentive-compatible) mechanism using at most $\operatorname{poly}(m)$ bits of communication that attains expected social welfare at least $(1/2 + \varepsilon) \max_{S \subseteq M} (v_1(S) + v_2(M \setminus S))$ on every pair of XOS valuations $(v_1, v_2)$?
literature.source_title: The Hardness of Dominant Strategy Mechanism Design, Revisited

literature.title: Tight deterministic DSIC approximation ratio for XOS combinatorial auctions
literature.statement: For an auction with $m$ items and parameter $\gamma \in [\log m, m]$, let $\mathsf{DSIC_{XOS}}(m, \gamma)$ denote the best social welfare approximation ratio attainable by a deterministic, individually rational, no-negative-transfers DSIC mechanism using at most $2^\gamma$ communication when bidders have XOS valuations. The paper proves a lower bound $\mathsf{DSIC_{XOS}}(m, \gamma) = \Omega((m/\gamma)^{1/5})$. Is the true optimal approximation ratio $\mathsf{DSIC_{XOS}}(m, \gamma) = \tilde{\Theta}((m/\gamma)^{1/2})$, matching the known bound for maximal-in-range truthful mechanisms, or can deterministic DSIC mechanisms achieve an approximation ratio $o((m/\gamma)^{1/2})$?

literature.title: Existence of a Strong Equilibrium in Unweighted Max-k-Cut Games
literature.statement: Let $G = (V, E)$ be a finite simple unweighted graph and let $k \ge 3$ be an integer. In the unweighted Max-$k$-Cut game on $(G, k)$, each player $v \in V$ chooses a strategy $\sigma(v) \in \{1, \dots, k\}$, and player $v$'s utility is $u_v(\sigma) = |\{w \in N(v) : \sigma(w) \neq \sigma(v)\}|$, where $N(v)$ denotes the open neighborhood of $v$ in $G$. A strong deviation from a strategy profile $\sigma: V \to \{1, \dots, k\}$ is a non-empty coalition $S \subseteq V$ and a profile $\tau: V \to \{1, \dots, k\}$ such that $\tau(v) = \sigma(v)$ for all $v \in V \setminus S$ and $u_v(\tau) > u_v(\sigma)$ for all $v \in S$. A profile $\sigma$ is a strong equilibrium if it admits no strong deviation. Does every finite simple unweighted graph admit a strong equilibrium in the Max-$k$-Cut game for every $k \ge 3$?
literature.source_title: Social Optimality Does Not Imply Coalitional Stability in Unweighted Max-k-Cut Games
literature.rationale: While the paper exhibits an unweighted graph where an optimal coloring admits a profitable coalitional deviation, the coalition deviates to another optimal coloring that may itself be stable, leaving the universal existence of strong equilibria unresolved.

literature.title: Maximum Degree Threshold for Coalitional Stability of Optimal Colorings
literature.statement: For an integer $k \ge 3$, let $\Delta^*(k)$ denote the largest integer $D$ such that for every finite simple unweighted graph $G = (V, E)$ with maximum degree $\Delta(G) \le D$, every cut-maximizing coloring $\sigma: V \to \{1, \dots, k\}$ in the unweighted Max-$k$-Cut game is a strong equilibrium. It is known that $\Delta^*(k) \ge 2k - 1$ (which gives $\Delta^*(3) \ge 5$). What is the exact value of $\Delta^*(k)$ for each $k \ge 3$, and in particular, what is the exact value of $\Delta^*(3)$?
literature.source_title: Social Optimality Does Not Imply Coalitional Stability in Unweighted Max-k-Cut Games
literature.rationale: Corollary 9 shows that every optimal coloring is a strong equilibrium whenever the maximum degree satisfies $\Delta(G) \le 2k - 1$ (recovering a known bound), while Theorem 2 provides a counterexample where $\Delta(G) > 2k - 1$. The paper leaves open the sharp maximum degree threshold separating graphs where all optimal colorings are coalitionally stable from those admitting unstable optima.

literature.title: Tight asymptotic threshold for MMS allocations with monotone goods
literature.statement: Let M be a set of m indivisible items and N = {1, ..., n} a set of n ≥ 2 agents. Each agent i ∈ N has a monotone valuation function v_i : 2^M → ℝ with v_i(∅) = 0 and v_i(S) ≤ v_i(T) whenever S ⊆ T ⊆ M. The maximin share of agent i is MMS(M, v_i, n) = max_{P} min_{j ∈ [n]} v_i(P_j), where the maximum is over all partitions P = (P_1, ..., P_n) of M into n bundles. An allocation A = (A_1, ..., A_n) of M is an MMS allocation if v_i(A_i) ≥ MMS(M, v_i, n) for all i ∈ N. Define μ(n) to be the largest integer m such that every instance with n agents, at most m goods, and monotone valuations has an MMS allocation. Is μ(n) = n + log_2 n + o(log_2 n) as n → ∞?
literature.source_title: On MMS allocations with few items
literature.rationale: The paper establishes that μ(n) = n + Θ(log n), showing the upper bound μ(n) ≤ n + log_2 n + O(log log n) in Theorem 6 and the lower bound μ(n) ≥ n + c log_2 n for c ≈ 0.93 in Lemma 9 and Lemma 8. Closing the gap to determine whether the leading constant is 1 remains open.

literature.title: Universal Constant for General-to-Internal Collage System Conversion
literature.source_title: A Factor-5 Conversion to Internal Collage Systems
literature.rationale: The paper proves an upper bound of $5m$ (and more precisely $4m+a-b$, where $a$ is the number of original truncation rules and $b$ is the breaker count) for converting an arbitrary collage system of size $m$ into an equivalent internal collage system. The proof intentionally allows worst-case helper charges to each lineage, suggesting that a tighter accounting could further reduce the constant.

literature.title: Existence of an optimal coloring that is a strong equilibrium in unweighted Max-k-Cut games
literature.statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple unweighted graph and $k\ge 3$. In the unweighted Max-$k$-Cut game each vertex picks a color in $\{1,\dots,k\}$ and its utility is the number of neighbours with a different color; a coloring is optimal if it maximizes the total utility (equivalently, the cut value), and a strong equilibrium if no nonempty coalition can jointly recolor so that every member strictly gains. Does every such game admit an optimal coloring that is a strong equilibrium? (Not every optimal coloring is one: arXiv:2610.04948, Theorem 2.)
literature.rationale: A positive answer implies existence of strong equilibria (OP-85); the paper's counterexample (Remark 6) does not rule out another, stable optimum on its graph. Optimal colorings are strong equilibria when the maximum degree is at most 2k-1.
